title: Medical Laboratory Scientist I, Chemistry - Part Time Weekend Nights
description:
Site: The General Hospital Corporation


Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.


Job Summary

We’re offering a generous sign-on bonus of $10,000 to eligible candidates who join our team. Recognizing and valuing exceptional talent, we’re excited to discuss the details of this bonus during the interview process.


Starting rate is $33/hour. Hourly pay is based on experience, education, and certifications, plus additional differentials, premiums, and incentives where applicable.

Summary:
This is a 3x8 shift night shift weekend role- Friday, Saturday, Sunday
11 PM to 7:30 AM

MUST be ASCP Certified or have proven eligibility from American Society for Clinical Pathology to test.

The Medical Laboratory Scientist I, in their role as Testing Personnel as defined by CLIA, are responsible for specimen processing, test performance, and for reporting waived and non-waived test results. Under general supervision, each individual performs only those tests that are authorized by the laboratory manager and require a degree of skill commensurate with the individual's education, training or experience, and technical abilities.


As outlined by CLIA, after successful completion of orientation, training, and competency assessment on all instruments/methods applicable to their role:
Follow the laboratory's procedures for specimen handling and processing, test analyses, reporting, and maintaining records of patient test results.
Maintain records that demonstrate that proficiency testing samples are tested in the same manner as patient samples.

Adhere to the laboratory's quality control policies, document all quality control activities, instrument and procedural calibrations, and maintenance performed.
Follow the laboratory's established corrective action policies and procedures whenever test systems are not within the laboratory's established acceptable levels of performance.

Be capable of identifying problems that may adversely affect test performance or reporting of test results and either must correct the problems or immediately notify the general supervisor, technical consultant, technical supervisor, clinical consultant, or director.

Document all corrective actions taken when test systems deviate from the laboratory's established performance specifications.


Qualifications

Education
Bachelor's Degree Clinical Laboratory Sciences required or Bachelor's Degree Medical Technology required or Bachelor's Degree Laboratory Sciences required

Licenses and Credentials
Medical Technologist (ASCP) - American Society for Clinical Pathology Board of Certification (ASCP-BOC) preferred

Experience
lab experience 1-2 years required

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
- Must have basic understanding of laboratory equipment and its operation, maintenance and repair and analytic techniques.
- Ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment.
- Must have the ability to pay careful attention to detail and to adhere to written protocols, including communication with supervisors when issues are identified.
- Must be able to perform as a team member.
- Excellent interpersonal skills.
- Ability to interact professionally and effectively with numerous staff including physicians, hospital personnel, employees, and patients.

Onsite


Work Location

90 Blossom Street


Scheduled Weekly Hours

24


Employee Type

Regular


Work Shift

Night (United States of America)



Pay Range

$33 - $40.70/Hourly

Grade

6


At Mass General Brigham, we believe in recognizing and rewarding the unique value each team member brings to our organization. Our approach to determining base pay is comprehensive, and any offer extended will take into account your skills, relevant experience if applicable, education, certifications and other essential factors. title: Research Assistant
description:
Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Our community is a close-knit group of remarkable individuals driven by intellectual inquiry, a commitment to social justice, and a shared dedication to making a difference in the world.

Requirements

Job Overview


We are hiring for a Research Assistant, Department of Oncology/Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center/Georgetown University Medical Center – Georgetown University. The person should be familiar with day-to-day assistance required in the laboratory such as ordering reagents, keeping inventories, autoclaving, knowledge of lab safety standards and their routine and timely inspection etc. In addition, the person should be able to carry out the laboratory techniques such as Western blotting, PCR, RT-PCR; should be conversant with tissue culture techniques. Being an immunology/immunotherapy lab, majority of work in the lab requires handling mice, including tumor implantation, injections, as well as collecting tissues and their processing. Therefore, experience in working with mice is desired or the person should be willing to get trained and work with mice. In addition, the person will be processing the samples collected from the patients on the clinical trials.

Work Interactions


The candidate would work in collaboration with the lab members and would report to Dr. Khleif and Dr. Gupta.

Requirements and Qualifications


  • Should have basic knowledge of cancer biology and various techniques used in this field of research with a High School Diploma or Associate degree and 1 year of experience.
  • A M.S. in Cell Biology/Immunology/Cancer Biology or B.S. (Biological Sciences) with relevant experience (1-2 years) would be preferred for this position

title: Family Care Specialist
description:
Join Us in Transforming Lives Every Day

At OneLegacy, every moment counts. As the nation's largest organ, eye, and tissue recovery organization, we are dedicated to saving lives and sharing hope. Guided by our values of integrity, compassion, stewardship, diversity and inclusion, urgency, innovation and excellence, and collaboration, our team works tirelessly to honor every gift of donation. This is more than a job; it’s an opportunity to make a profound impact on countless lives.

Job Type: Full-time, Non-exempt

Work Hours: Shifts are 12 hour shifts; 11am-11pm. Assigned days and/or shift can be changed according to staffing needs. Must be available evenings, holidays, and weekends as required, and also includes overtime.

Work Setting: In-person and Field Service Area

Location: Orange, CA

Travel: Required to travel by personal auto or air to meeting sites and other locations.

Summary of Functions:

The Family Care Specialist is Responsible for representing OneLegacy to the potential donor’s Authorizing Party and family. Works in collaboration with the hospital treatment team to develop a timely and sensitive approach plan. The Family Care Specialist approaches the Authorizing Party and family for organ, eye, and tissue authorization, providing support and information while maintaining a position of dual advocacy to donor family and hospital staff. Acts as a liaison between hospital staff and OneLegacy.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Essential Job Functions:

Family Care and Authorization:

  1. Work in partnership with the hospital staff and OneLegacy to ensure that the Authorizing Party is identified per UAGA guidelines.
  2. Collaborate with the hospital care team and OneLegacy staff through frequent huddles to ensure the Authorizing Party is presented the opportunity for donation in the most appropriate manner.
  3. Discuss the elements of authorization with Authorizing Party and/or family members of potential donors.
  4. Obtain authorization for donation per UAGA and verify the medical-legal documentation necessary for organ recovery is completed according to OneLegacy policies and procedures.
  5. Work with hospital and OneLegacy staff to obtain administrative authorization for donation when appropriate.
  6. Support the donor family through the donation process including any internal or external resources.
  7. Proficiently and accurately enter data into Digital Donor.
  8. Complete Donor Medical and Social History Questionnaire (DMSHQ) and obtain any follow-up information required.

Referral Response and Authorization:

  1. Respond promptly and appropriately to potential donor referrals to assess family dynamics, donor suitability and to enhance the referral and authorization process.
  2. Review donor suitability with Referral Management team, inform hospital staff of outcome and create plan to follow.
  3. Collaborate with the hospital staff to determine and locate the Authorizing Party.
  4. Acts as a liaison between hospital staff and patient’s family.
  5. Proficiently and accurately enter data into Digital Donor.
  6. Performs potential donor evaluation on-sites when requested by Clinical Resource Specialists.

Professional Education:

  1. Provide education to hospital staff on the benefits of organ and tissue donation and services provided by OneLegacy to grieving families.
  2. Participate in public education forums as requested.
  3. Provide educational materials (e.g. placards, phone stickers, newsletters) to appropriate hospital units.
  4. Provide education to hospital staff about authorization and family care process.

Job Qualifications and Requirements:

Education: Four (4) year Bachelor’s degree or one (1) year applicable OPO (organ procurement organization) experience. Documented education in grief counseling required

Experience: Customer service; bilingual preferred.

Certification/License:OneLegacy requires employees to maintain a current California driver’s license and current vehicle insurance based on California minimum insurance coverage standards.

Salary Range: $71,662.50 - $79,625

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, OneLegacy considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

  • 19 days of PTO

  • 10 Holidays

  • Gym Onsite

  • Tuition Reimbursement

  • School Loan Forgiveness

title: Senior AI Product Designer  (m/w/d)
description:
About Recare

As one of the leading German HealthTech companies, we are reshaping discharge management – technology-driven, patient-centered, and free from bureaucracy. In addition to our market-leading SaaS platform, we develop AI solutions that radically simplify processes in hospitals and for aftercare providers, relieve healthcare professionals, and refocus attention on patients. Today, we already connect two-thirds of all German hospitals with over 650 rehabilitation clinics and 25,000 nursing and homecare providers. With currently around 100 employees, we continue to grow – and we are looking for people with character who want to help us improve the healthcare system and solve administrative complexity across care journeys in Europe.

What you'll own as our Senior AI Product Designer

  • You'll own end-to-end design for one of our core product areas, on a platform where AI is the foundation of the product, not a bolt-on feature. Your mission is to bring consumer-grade craft to a B2B healthcare product used by clinicians and hospital administrators under real time pressure, and to help invent the design patterns for AI-native surfaces that don't exist anywhere else yet.

  • You design the AI-native surfaces our platform is built around, including multi-modal interfaces, agent state, uncertainty, and human-in-the-loop controls, inventing the patterns as you go rather than adapting existing ones.

  • You own end-to-end design for a product area – Discharge Core, Voice Desktop, Extract & Docs, Patient Overview, or Agent – taking work from a messy problem statement through to what ships in production.

  • You contribute to our design system, building the components and AI-specific conventions that other designers and teams build on.

  • You partner closely with product and engineering, shaping technical and product direction rather than being handed a spec to execute against.

    You work with other designers across the organisation, bringing your input and influence beyond your own product area rather than staying inside a single team's boundary.

  • You hold a high craft bar in critique, lifting the standard of what the wider design team ships.

You help hold coherence across our AI Suite (Voice, Docs, Extract, Agent) and Discharge Core, so a fast-growing multi-product platform still feels like one product to the people using it.

How we design:

  • We're AI-native. We use AI tools daily in our own process, not just in what we design, and we want strong, opinionated views on how to wield them well.

  • Consumer-grade craft is the bar, even in B2B. Our users are clinicians and hospital administrators.

  • Human-in-the-loop by default. This is healthcare: AI proposes, people stay in control, and we design the approval and verification moments that make that real, not just a confidence score bolted on.

  • We ship in production, not just in Figma. Craft is judged by what clinicians actually use, so we stay close to what ships.

What to expect as our Senior AI Product Designer (m/w/d):

  • Purposeful work – your role will have a positive impact on patients, their families, and healthcare professionals.

  • Company culture – we believe in flat hierarchies that promote high performance and strong team dynamics. We foster an environment characterized by mutual respect, loyalty, and recognition. Together, we strive for our goals – and expect the same from you.

  • Flexibility – want to pick up your child from daycare? Like to exercise during lunch? We'll support you. We are a remote-friendly company offering flexible working hours. Workations are also possible by arrangement.

  • Edenred card – which you can use according to your needs.

  • Extra vacation day – so you can celebrate your birthday with your loved ones, you'll have the day off.

Requirements

Here's how we picture you as our Senior AI Product Designer (m/w/d):

  • You have 8+ years of product design experience, with at least 3+ years operating at Senior, Principal, or Staff altitude.

  • You have designed for AI and non-determinism before, and can talk concretely about how you've communicated agent behaviour, handled errors, and kept users in control, not just in the abstract.

  • You have owned or significantly contributed to a design system, at the level of patterns and principles rather than individual components.

  • You are block-shaped: equally strong across UX process, UI craft, product thinking, research, storytelling, and cross-functional collaboration.

  • You have taken features from 0 to 1 through an ambiguous problem statement to shipped code, and you're comfortable feeling like a PM or frontend developer on the days that calls for it.

  • You have high agency and spot gaps without being asked to look for them, including outside your own product area.

  • You hold a position under pressure but change it when new information warrants, rather than becoming precious about your own decisions.

  • You communicate confidently in English and are comfortable operating in an international environment; German is a plus but not required.

  • You bring a consumer-grade craft background with exceptional design; healthtech experience is a plus but not required.

  • If this sounds like your kind of challenge, we'd love to hear from you

Contract Type: Specific purpose contract (2 years)

Location: Villa Park (with requirements to travel to and from community sessions)

The Department

The Aston Villa Foundation is the official Charity of Aston Villa Football Club and prides itself in being innovative in its approach to the club being used as a ‘Force for Good’.

Disability Football and physical activity is a long-standing Department, which compliments the Foundation’s 2024-28 Strategic Plan. The Disability department brings together several special educational needs and disability strands, all of which contribute to providing a landscape of opportunities for children and young people in a variety of education, development and learning settings.

The Role

The SEND coordinator role is an existing role for an experienced project/programme coordinator, with a proven track record in designing, coordinating, delivering and executing impactful projects with a special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) focus. This is a rapidly developing and exciting specialist area of provision, within a busy and growing charitable organisation with a strong reputation.

The SEND Coordinator will report to the Senior Programmes Manager (Engagement, Sport and Wellbeing) and will support the Disability Football Manager to coordinate/lead a team of full-time and part-time officers and coaches. They will support them in the delivery of excellent, impactful projects, activities and programmes whilst also identifying and developing new opportunities to widen our impact and the development of our people with special educational needs and disabilities.

For further information about the Role, please see the Role profile

The Person

The Aston Villa Foundation is seeking a highly skilled, driven and purposeful SEND Coordinator with a genuine interest in charitable and community work.

You will be experienced and proficient in the delivery of special educational needs and disabilities activities, programmes and events, coordinating people, projects and programmes, and have a strong track record of partnership working and collaborating with key stakeholders and experienced in developing new project/service opportunities in your chosen field.

At the same time, you can expect flexibility in the role, autonomy and a commitment to professional development, inside a vibrant and rewarding working environment.

title: Senior Managing Director, Head of IG Fixed Income
location: United States, Chesterfield, MO, RGA HQ
description:
You desire impactful work.

You’re RGA ready

RGA is a purpose-driven organization working to solve today’s challenges through innovation and collaboration. A Fortune 200 Company and listed among its World’s Most Admired Companies, we’re the only global reinsurance company to focus primarily on life- and health-related solutions. Join our multinational team of intelligent, motivated, and collaborative people, and help us make financial protection accessible to all.

A Brief Overview


RGA’s global Investments team manages more than $145 billion in assets and includes over 290 associates with a local presence around the world. Built on a globally integrated platform that combines liability expertise, proprietary capabilities, strategic partnerships, and disciplined execution, Investments delivers tailored solutions that support RGA’s financial strength, flexibility, and competitive advantage. The team balances risk and return to maintain a diversified, resilient, and high-quality investment portfolio aligned with the needs of RGA, its clients, and partners. Through a flexible asset platform and broad suite of investment capabilities, Investments serves as a strategic partner in supporting RGA’s long-term success.

This Senior Managing Director is a senior leader and member of the Investment leadership team, a group responsible for the strategic direction of RGA’s $150B general account investment portfolio and its integral role in RGA’s success. · Partner closely with Investment Solutions, Global Portfolio Management, Risk, Finance, and regional investment leaders to align investment strategies with enterprise objectives.

· Build, develop, and retain high-performing teams, fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, intellectual rigor, continuous improvement, and accountability.

· Evaluate and evolve organizational structures, talent strategies, and operating models to support growth, scalability, efficiency, and future investment platform needs.

· Serve as a strategic partner to executive leadership and business stakeholders, ensuring investment strategies support business objectives, new business initiatives, and enterprise priorities.

· Represent the investment platform with senior leadership, boards, regulators, rating agencies, clients, and external partners, providing thought leadership and influencing strategic decisions.

Innovation & Platform Modernization

· Champion the modernization of the investment platform through technology, data, automation, and artificial intelligence, driving innovation, operational excellence, and enhanced investment decision-making

A Senior Solution Designer is needed to support 6 projects within the Geospatial Ontario IT Program.

    1. This is an annually reoccurring maintenance project for the GIS Delivery Platform (GDP). Work this fiscal will focus on software patching, Portal for ArcGIS implementation, Geocortex to VertiGIS migration, Cyber Security analysis/mitigations, and platform architecture review/documentation.
  2. GIS Delivery Platform Modernization FY24-25 (11% allocation or 15 days of effort)
    1. This is a GIS infrastructure modernization project focused on implementing modern platform monitoring, analytics, and reporting middleware.

    1. This is a bi-annually reoccurring maintenance project for the GIS Delivery Platform (GDP). Work this fiscal will focus on software patching, FME, ArcGIS Server, Oracle, etc. upgrades.

    1. LIO Editor/Mapper/Reporter toolset is a legacy GIS data maintenance solution owned by Geospatial Ontario. This project aims to perform a modernization options analysis, then create / recommend a solution design.

    1. This project aims to modernize the legacy LIO Editor GIS data maintenance solution. This is an implementation project for procuring new GIS infrastructure, configuring middleware, building editing tools, procedures, and following Ontario Government IT governance standards.

title: Workday Integration Developer
description:
What you’ll do


Reporting to the Chapter Manager, Workday & HR Platforms, the Workday Integration Developer designs, builds, tests, deploys, and supports integrations across Canadian Tire Corporation’s Workday ecosystem.


This role enables secure and reliable HR data movement between Workday and connected enterprise systems, including payroll, benefits, time and absence, workforce management, identity management, reporting, external vendors, and downstream applications.


As part of the Workday & HR Platforms team, this role contributes to integration solution design, technical configuration, development, testing, production deployment, and ongoing support. The Workday Integration Developer partners with HR, Technology, Payroll, Benefits, Workforce Management, Security, Reporting, Solutions Architecture, and vendor teams to deliver scalable, compliant, and supportable HR platform solutions.


  • Design, build, configure, test, deploy, and support inbound and outbound Workday integrations that enable critical HR, payroll, benefits, time and absence, workforce, security, reporting, and vendor data flows across Canadian Tire Corporation.
  • Develop and enhance integrations using Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB), Core Connectors, Workday Studio, Report-as-a-Service (RaaS), custom reports, calculated fields, Document Transformation, and Workday Web Services.
  • Translate business and functional requirements into technical integration designs, data mappings, transformation logic, test plans, deployment plans, and support documentation.
  • Provide production support for scheduled and event-driven integrations, including monitoring, alert review, incident triage, error analysis, file delivery validation, and stakeholder communication.
  • Troubleshoot integration failures, data discrepancies, authentication issues, file transmission errors, and vendor-reported defects; perform root cause analysis and implement sustainable fixes.
  • Implement secure data exchange patterns, including integration system users, domain security, security groups, PGP encryption, SFTP, web services, certificates, and least-privilege access principles.
  • Partner with HR functional teams, HR Employee Services, Payroll, Benefits, Time and Absence, Workforce Management, Talent, Reporting, Information Security, Enterprise Technology, Solutions Architecture, and vendors to deliver supportable integration solutions.
  • Create and maintain integration design documents, mapping specifications, runbooks, support procedures, test evidence, issue logs, release notes, and knowledge base content.
  • Support Workday release readiness by assessing release notes, coordinating regression testing, validating impacted integrations, documenting outcomes, and resolving release-related defects.
  • Participate in change, incident, problem, audit, privacy, and production deployment activities in alignment with CTC governance and operational standards.

What you bring:

  • 3 - 5 years of hands-on experience developing, enhancing, testing, deploying, and supporting Workday integrations in a production HR technology environment.
  • Practical experience with Workday integration capabilities such as EIB, Core Connectors, Workday Studio, RaaS, custom reports, calculated fields, Document Transformation, and Workday Web Services.
  • Strong understanding of integration concepts and technologies, including XML, XSLT, XPath, SOAP, REST, JSON, SFTP, PGP encryption, authentication, certificates, scheduling, logging, transformation logic, and error handling.
  • Experience translating business requirements into technical integration specifications, data mappings, transformation rules, test cases, deployment steps, and operational support guidance.
  • Experience with Workday HCM functional areas such as Core HCM, Time Tracking, Absence, Benefits, Recruiting, Learning, Workday Scheduling, payroll processes, or Workforce Management.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot production issues by reviewing integration events, analyzing logs, validating source and target data, identifying root causes, and implementing sustainable fixes.
  • Understanding of Workday security concepts, including integration system users, security groups, domain security policies, business process security, and role-based access controls.
  • Experience working within formal IT practices, including incident, change, release, testing, audit support, and operational documentation.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills, with the ability to translate technical details into support procedures, stakeholder updates, test plans, and knowledge base materials.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, prioritization, and attention-to-detail skills, with a commitment to data quality, privacy, compliance, operational stability, and secure handling of sensitive employee information.
  • Experience in a large Canadian enterprise, retail, distribution centre, hourly workforce, or multi-banner environment is considered an asset.
  • Knowledge of Dayforce is preferred and considered an asset but is not mandatory.
  • Workday Pro Orchestration Developer, Workday Pro Studio, or other relevant technical certification is considered an asset.

title: Analyst/Sr Analyst, Machinery & Equipment Appraisals
description:
About Gordon Brothers:
Since 1903, Gordon Brothers has helped companies unlock the potential of their assets. Our solutions-oriented approach combined with over 120 years of industry knowledge enables clients to get the most value from their assets with tailored solutions across asset services, asset lending and financing, and asset trading. Leveraging our deep expertise in retail, industrial, brands and real estate, we work closely with clients globally to determine the value of, lend against, or buy and sell their assets to help them achieve their business goals.

At Gordon Brothers, we foster a culture of collaboration and creativity to find unique and innovative solutions for our clients. We take pride in fostering an engaging, inclusive culture and encouraging employees to bring new ideas to the table, develop their skills, and build dynamic and fulfilling careers.

For more information, please visit www.gordonbrothers.com.



Description

Our ideal candidate will be located in NY or Michigan to service clients in those areas. The machinery and equipment (M&E) appraiser plays a critical role in asset-based lending (ABL) by determining the realizable value of equipment that will serve as collateral for a loan. Gordon Brothers’ valuation teams specifically value machinery and equipment for lending purposes and provide lenders with an independent assessment of collateral value to support borrowing base calculations and credit decisions. The Analyst is responsible for data collection and analysis for preparing the appraisal report, including conducting client on-site inspections, due diligence, management interviews, company and industry research, and narrative report writing per USPAP standards, as they apply to Machinery & Equipment valuations.

Job Responsibilities/Essential Job Functions

  • Participates in on-the-job training to learn fundamental Machinery & Equipment terminology, concepts, practices, and procedures to conduct a typical Machinery & Equipment valuation engagement.
  • Reviews previously performed models and completed appraisal reports to gain an understanding of the valuation process and concepts.
  • Participates in travel for job inspections, and/or client meetings with or without another Analyst or Appraiser, including taking photographs of assets during site inspections and providing notes and equipment listings.
  • Provides analytical and research support for projects as assigned, including company and industry analysis and research on key performance indicators to help determine value.
  • Works in accordance with established methodologies and processes with direction from a project manager.
  • Communicates directly, as instructed, with bank clients and appraised companies to understand company-provided information and operational challenges.
  • Develops a qualitative understanding of nuances that may affect values, and reviews findings with company management and clients.
  • Assists to produce a final appraisal report of quantitative and qualitative findings.
  • Maintains Gordon Brothers’ Appraisal Application database to ensure accurate and timely contact, company, and project information.
  • Learns and adheres to USPAP standards, as they apply to Machinery & Equipment valuations.

title: Senior Computer Systems Engineer/Architect - Informatica
description:
Overview

Nakupuna Companies is seeking a Senior Computer Systems Engineer/Architect with Informatica expertise to join our team of talented consultants. The individual will provide solution architecture execution strategy for the Informatica implementation in NAVSUP AWS GovCloud. This role is responsible for the cross-platform design, Everything as Code approach, security architecture, availability and recovery strategy, CI/CD practices, technical integration decisions, and day-to-day engineering coordination needed to move the solution from architecture through production sustainment.

The individual will support NAVSUP Business Systems Center as the senior solution architect for the design, integration, testing, deployment, documentation, and sustainment of the Informatica Data Governance Suite within NAVSUP’s AWS GovCloud environment. Develop the cross-platform architecture and engineering standards for high availability, disaster recovery, security, Everything as Code, CI/CD, monitoring, configuration management, and change control. Coordinate technical activities across the Informatica, database, cloud, cybersecurity, and testing workstreams; identify architecture dependencies and risks; and ensure technical artifacts are secure, reproducible, supportable, and ready for Government review. Support RMF/ATO activities, performance and capacity planning, operational readiness, and knowledge transfer to NAVSUP personnel.

Responsibilities

The following reflects management's definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign additional duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to mission requirements and reasonable accommodation.

  • Develop the high-availability architecture recommendation and agile prototype, including component sizing, dependencies, network design, compute, storage, load balancing, capacity, and cost considerations.
  • Define reliability objectives, RTO and RPO targets, failover strategies, backup and retention methods, restoration procedures, disaster-recovery tests, and rollback plans.
  • Lead the Everything as Code approach across infrastructure, configuration, security, governance policy, testing, and CI/CD deployment; ensure artifacts are reproducible and retained in Government version control.
  • Design AWS GovCloud resources and controls, including EC2, S3, networking, routing, security groups, load balancers, IAM roles, service accounts, logging, monitoring, and approved encryption.
  • Establish technical standards for source control, branching, peer review, automated testing, automated deployment, configuration management, and change control.
  • Lead security engineering for PKI, SSO, LDAP, OCSP, certificates, RBAC, least privilege, Zero Trust, logging, vulnerability remediation, and integration with NAVSUP security operations.
  • Coordinate RMF/ATO and STIG compliance activities, including control mappings, diagrams, system-security documentation, hardening evidence, POA&M inputs, retesting, and closure support.
  • Guide Informatica platform architecture, data integration, performance testing, interoperability, and operational-readiness decisions across the team.
  • Review and approve internal technical designs, scripts, code, configurations, tests, diagrams, runbooks, and deployment packages for quality, consistency, security, and supportability.
  • Establish continuous monitoring for availability, performance, errors, capacity, cost, API metrics, and data-quality indicators using CloudWatch, Splunk, AppDynamics, Informatica, or comparable tools.
  • Coordinate technical risk management, issue resolution, root-cause analysis, vendor coordination, sprint planning, milestone reviews, Government briefings, and stakeholder decision support.
  • Plan and deliver hands-on knowledge transfer so NAVSUP administrators and engineers can operate, maintain, recover, and enhance the solution.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned

Qualifications

Skills/Qualifications:

In addition to being able to confidently perform the above job duties, the candidate should demonstrate the following:

  • Technical Leadership - Provides clear day-to-day direction across Informatica, AWS, security, testing, and sustainment work; reviews designs and engineering artifacts critically and resolves cross-platform risks before they reach production.
  • Agile / DevSecOps - Turns architecture into prioritized, testable work with clear dependencies, acceptance criteria, and decision points; establishes repeatable source-control, peer-review, automated-testing, and CI/CD practices.
  • Analytical / Problem Solving - Balances mission needs, security, reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, cost, and long-term supportability; uses evidence and prototypes to resolve uncertainty and clearly frames options for Government decisions.
  • Communication / Teamwork - Communicates technical issues, risks, and tradeoffs in terms that both engineers and Government leaders can act on; creates a collaborative environment across a small multidisciplinary team and external stakeholders.
  • Quality / Coaching - Sets and enforces standards for architecture, code, configuration, tests, diagrams, runbooks, and security evidence; builds Government ownership through practical mentoring, recorded walkthroughs, and current sustainment documentation.

Education and Experience:

Education: A bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, cybersecurity, or a related technical field is preferred.

Required experience: The candidate must be able to demonstrate the following:

  • 7 years of hands-on Informatica experience
  • 10 years of senior-level experience architecting working with enterprise platforms in AWS or AWS GovCloud from design through production operations.
  • Strong knowledge of cloud computing, storage, networking, security groups, load balancing, identity and access management, encryption, monitoring, performance, capacity, and cost optimization.
  • Experience implementing Infrastructure as Code, Configuration as Code, Security or Policy as Code, automated testing, Git-based version control, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience designing high availability, backup, disaster recovery, RTO/RPO, failover, restoration testing, and rollback for production systems.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise API, data-integration, data-governance, metadata, data-quality, and relational data-warehouse architectures.
  • Strong knowledge of RMF/ATO, STIGs, NIST 800-53 controls, system hardening, PKI, SSO, RBAC, logging, vulnerability remediation, and Zero Trust concepts.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead a small multidisciplinary engineering team and work directly with Government technical, security, contracting, and program stakeholders.
  • Ability to review technical work critically, resolve cross-platform issues, manage risk, and maintain clear architecture and operational documentation.
  • U.S. citizenship and ability to meet all privileged-access, background-investigation, CAC, SAAR, training, certification, and NDA requirements.

Preferred experience: The following experience will strengthen the candidate's fit for this role:

  • Recent AWS GovCloud architecture and DevSecOps experience supporting DoD or other Federal production systems.
  • AWS Solutions Architect Professional, AWS DevOps Engineer Professional, AWS Security Specialty, or comparable current certification.
  • Experience with Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, Ansible, or comparable IaC/CaC tooling and Azure DevOps repositories and pipelines.
  • Architecture or technical-lead experience involving MuleSoft Anypoint Platform and Informatica Enterprise Data Catalog, Axon, Data Quality, or PowerCenter.
  • Experience integrating CloudWatch, Splunk, AppDynamics, or comparable observability platforms with enterprise applications.
  • Prior experience with Navy data, WDP/Jupiter, Flank Speed, Microsoft Power Platform, logistics systems, or Government API-management initiatives.

Certifications:

Required: Current DoD 8140.03 IAT Level II baseline certification at the start of performance: CompTIA Security+ CE or a PWS-listed substitute (CCNA, CySA+, GICSP, GSEC, or CND).

Required within six months: An applicable computing-environment certification in AWS, Windows, Oracle, UNIX, or Linux, coordinated to the assigned environment.

Clearance and access: This position requires U.S. citizenship, CAC eligibility, and a final, favorably adjudicated T5, T5R, SSBI, or equivalent investigation before privileged access is granted. Interim privileged access is authorized. The certification requirements stated above also apply.

Soft Skills

  • Effective communication with development, operations, and security teams.
  • Ability to advocate for security best practices in a DevOps culture.

Desirable Skills

Containerization Security

  • Expertise in Kubernetes security (e.g., RBAC, network policies, pod security standards, secrets management).
  • Knowledge of container runtime security (e.g., container escapes, rootless containers, sandboxing).
  • Image security best practices, including scanning, signing, and provenance verification.
  • Secure deployment patterns using Tanzu & Kubernetes.
  • Runtime security monitoring.

DevSecOps & CI/CD Security

  • Secure CI/CD pipeline design with security testing using like Git and SonarQube.
  • Implementation of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) security (e.g., Terraform, Ansible).
  • Secrets management in CI/CD pipelines using Vault or Kubernetes Secrets.
  • Security automation and policy enforcement using tools like GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and Jenkins.

Cloud & Infrastructure Security

  • Strong knowledge of cloud security principles in a containerised environment.
  • Kubernetes security posture management (KSPM) using tools like Trivy.
  • Secure ingress/egress controls, service mesh security (e.g., Istio).
  • Encryption strategies for data at rest, in transit, and in use.
  • Network security best practices for Tanzu container networking (e.g., NSX, Rancher)
  • Compliance monitoring and security auditing for cloud-native environments.

Automation & Scripting

  • Scripting skills in Python, PowerShell for security automation.
  • API security knowledge (e.g., OAuth, JWT, API gateways, rate limiting).
  • Experience with Security as Code for automated policy enforcement.

title: Security Staff
description:
At Boxcar, our product is a good time. For us, that means cold drinks, exciting games, great pizza, and even better people.

Boxcar has four locations across North Carolina. We’re not a chain. We value personality. What ties each spot together is a team that cares deeply about making each guest’s night a great one and looking out for one another.

Our vibe is eclectic, sometimes eccentric, but always welcoming. Our customers are a mix of pinball regulars, after-work crews, party-goers, competitive skee-ballers, and folks who just want a smooth drink in a place that doesn’t take itself too seriously.

Our Security Staff are the peacekeepers. We aren't looking for bouncers on a power trip. We are looking for professionals who know that the best security is a conversation, not a confrontation. You ensure our guests and employees stay safe, the vibe stays fun, and the wrong people stay out.

  • Man the door. You are the first impression. Greet guests, check IDs, and perform thorough screenings to ensure no weapons or outside alcohol enter the building.
  • De-escalate first. Your mouth is your best weapon. We expect you to diffuse tension and talk people down rather than rile them up. Adhere to our policies on use of force and de-escalation.
  • Handle the heat. When words fail, you act. Safely and professionally remove guests who are intoxicated, aggressive, or threatening the safety of others.
  • Communicate. Keep your earpiece in and your head on a swivel. Clear, professional communication with the team via walkie-talkie is how we prevent issues before they start. When necessary to contact local police, you’ll do so.
  • Document everything. If an incident occurs, you work with management to save camera footage and complete detailed ‘Incident Reports’.
  • Support the team. If the door is quiet and the floor is messy, you help bus glassware or clear trash. We don’t just stand around with our arms crossed.
Our Non-Negotiables
  • No a**holes. We value kindness, honesty, integrity, and consideration. If you can’t abide by that, Boxcar isn’t the place for you.
  • One team, one dream. We don’t do silos or pass the buck. Pitch in and help out, even if it’s not your core responsibility. No job is too small.
What Else We’re Looking For
  • Experience. Minimum of 2 years related security experience. Prior military or law enforcement experience is a huge plus.
  • Judgment. You have the ability to make sound decisions under pressure.
  • Conscientiousness. You take the job seriously, but you don’t take yourself too seriously.
  • Genuine hospitability. You like people, and it shows in how you work.
  • Reliability. Full stop. Show up, on time, every time.
  • Physical presence. You are able to stand/walk for 8-hour shifts and have the ability to lift/carry/push over 100 lbs when needed.
  • Availability. You are ready to work nights and weekends, as that is when the business needs you most.
We’re not a corporate bar group. We’re a locally-owned business that cares about getting the details right for our people. Here’s what that means for you:
  • A culture you actually like. We aim to foster an environment where people want to work. We treat adults like adults, but don’t forget to have fun like kids.
  • We’ll have your back. The no a**holes policy applies to customers as well.
  • Growth opportunities. This doesn’t have to be the last job you have at Boxcar. We want to invest in your career. We prefer to promote from within and find ways to keep our best people around.
  • And the perks. 50% pizza discount, after-shift drink, competitive benefits available, and a workplace that is literally an arcade.
If you made it this far, let’s hear from you! Apply now.

About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. About this role:

The Finance Specialist, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) drives the planning, forecasting and performance-analysis cycle for a Carrier manufacturing facility. Working with general supervision on assignments that require judgment and interpretation, this role turns operational and financial data into insight that supports decision-making, cost control and profitable growth.

  • Leads the monthly forecast, annual operating plan (AOP) and long-range planning cycles for the site.
  • Performs month-end close activities, including accruals, journal entries and account reconciliations.

  • Partners with Operations, Materials and Engineering to track productivity, savings and cost-reduction initiatives.
  • Supports capital investment (CAPEX) requests with business cases, ROI and payback analysis.

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field.

  • Strong variance analysis skills with the ability to explain financial results to non-finance partners.
  • Advanced Excel and financial-modeling capability.
  • Working knowledge of US GAAP, internal controls and SOX compliance.
  • Experience with ERP systems and financial reporting tools.
  • Manufacturing or plant-finance experience, including standard costing and absorption analysis.
  • Proficiency with ERP (SAP/Oracle) and BI tools (Power BI, Hyperion/OneStream).

-

title: Equipment Reliability Leader
description:
We are the people who give possibilities purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.





Job Description

The Equipment Reliability Leader is responsible for achieving high-level asset reliability while optimizing costs through the development and implementation of a site-wide reliability program. This role involves leading a team of equipment reliability engineers, controls and vision technicians, and machine designers, with oversight of the tool room. The Equipment Reliability Leader will build effective communication with other teams (e.g., PM team, Product Line team) and coordinate ongoing internal projects and activities for priority assets to ensure an optimal maintenance plan is developed to address weak components and eliminate repetitive/costly breakdowns, continuously optimizing assets.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Implement reliability centered maintenance strategy, provide leadership and expertise to reliability team and beyond to ensure eradication of significant and repetitive breakdowns, achieve high reliability and lower cost.

  • Responsible for the site equipment classification evaluation and the definition of site maintenance strategies, procedures, and methods, aligning with maintenance budget and equipment classification.

  • Maintains effective partnership and supports Product Line and PM teams to diagnose high-complexity breakdowns and provide coaching during root-cause investigation promoting reliability tools & techniques.

  • Ensures harmonization of processes, promotes, and enforces technical standards maintaining up-to-date knowledge and awareness of improvement methodologies and new techniques in maintenance.

  • Ensures optimal availability, maintainability, and reliability of new equipment as well as assets documentation, including manuals, schemes and other related documents, maintenance plans.

  • Monitor and control site Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF), failure trends and maintenance costs to identify priorities, possible asset modification or decommissioning required.

  • Benchmark engineering and Maintenance results against other BD sites and external references.

title: Research Fellow (Organic Chemistry)
description:
The School of Chemistry, Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology (CCEB) conducts interdisciplinary education and research across chemistry, chemical engineering and biotechnology, with research strengths that include synthetic, biological and medicinal chemistry.

We are looking for a Research Fellow in Organic Chemistry to develop, synthesize, characterize and purify antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), peptides and related linker-payload components. The role will focus on solution-phase synthesis, solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), conjugation and purification workflows, analytical characterization, and the delivery of reproducible research results.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and execute multi-step solution-phase organic synthesis and solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) of peptides, linkers, payloads, linker-payloads and other ADC-related molecules.
  • Develop and optimize amide-bond formation and conjugation reactions, including coupling-reagent selection, protecting-group strategies, chemoselectivity, conversion and yield.
  • Develop and optimize ADC conjugation and purification workflows to produce material that meets project specifications.
  • Purify peptides, small molecules, intermediates, linker-payloads and ADCs using flash chromatography, preparative HPLC, SEC/FPLC and other suitable methods.
  • Characterize products and assess identity, purity, drug-to-antibody ratio and aggregation using NMR, LC-MS, HPLC/UPLC, UV-Vis, SEC and HIC.
  • Troubleshoot amide coupling, SPPS, conjugation, purification and analytical issues, and recommend practical solutions.
  • Maintain accurate experimental records and prepare technical reports, presentations and manuscripts.
  • Maintain good research and laboratory safety practices and perform related duties assigned by the Principal Investigator.

Job Requirements:

  • PhD in Chemistry, Chemical Biology or Biochemistry.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience in synthetic organic chemistry and in the synthesis and purification of antibody-drug conjugates; linker-payload chemistry and bioconjugation experience is required.
  • Hands-on experience with SPPS, including resin handling, coupling cycles, cleavage, deprotection, preparative HPLC purification and LC-MS analysis.
  • Experience developing amide-bond formation and conjugation methods, including coupling-reagent selection, protecting-group strategies, reaction optimization and chemoselectivity.
  • Experience with ADC purification and characterization using SEC/FPLC, HIC, LC-MS, analytical HPLC/UPLC and UV-Vis, including assessment of purity, drug-to-antibody ratio and aggregation.
  • Good experimental documentation, problem-solving, scientific writing and oral communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary research team.

We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

title: Program Manager - Airport Screening Operations
description:
Leidos is seeking a Program Manager to lead execution of a TSA Screening Partnership Program (SPP) task order providing airport security screening services at Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport (ROC). The Program Manager serves as the primary point of contact for all coordination and communication with the TSA Contracting Officer (CO) and Federal Security Director (FSD) or designee, and holds overall responsibility for screening operations, staffing, compliance, quality, and subcontractor management under the task order.


Leidos' Homeland Sector's Airports, Borders, and Security (ABS) business area delivers air travel modernization, border protection, and critical infrastructure security solutions that help build a safer, more resilient homeland. Operating globally across aviation security, passenger screening, cybersecurity, and border and port security, ABS integrates next-generation technologies to secure the movement of people and goods worldwide.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for all coordination and communication with the CO and/or FSD or designee at ROC.
  • Be available 24 hours a day, every day, to receive and implement orders or special instructions from the CO, COR, and/or FSD or designee within the scope of the contract concerning matters affecting the operation, protection, or screening of assigned areas.
  • Manage the total work associated with providing security screening services, meeting TSA's performance objectives for program management, workforce management, equipment maintenance and materials management, reporting, responsiveness, customer service, quality control, subcontractor management, and safety/health compliance.
  • Provide overall leadership for aviation security screening operations, ensuring compliance with contract requirements, TSA regulations, and federal aviation security standards.
  • Direct day-to-day management of screening operations, staffing levels, scheduling, and shift flexibility across passenger and baggage checkpoints.
  • Own the Operational Summary Plan and Report and weekly actuals reporting, briefing the FSD or designee on strategy-vs-execution differences within required timeframes.
  • Monitor and report program performance against the Contractor Performance Management Plan (CPMP) and Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs); respond to Contractor Improvement Reports (CIRs) and submit Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) as needed.
  • Establish and oversee the Contractor's pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, random, and post-accident drug and alcohol testing program for all screening personnel, consistent with 14 CFR Part 120 and 49 CFR Part 40.
  • Direct the organizational structure for the task order, including management of subcontractor personnel/roles and the overall quality control/quality assurance approach for screening operations.
  • Own compliance oversight for the task order's Information Technology Acquisition Review requirements (RMF/ATO, continuous monitoring, incident reporting, PIV/HSPD-12, staff training/NDA tracking), SSI safeguarding, and the Continuity of Operations (COOP) Plan and annual COOP exercise, or delegate to named leads.
  • Lead recruitment/retention strategy for the screening workforce, including staffing risk mitigation for background-check/vetting lead times that cannot be shortened.
  • Coordinate implementation of TSA best practices adopted for ROC (non-uniformed supervisor role, in-queue monitor, Dual-Function Screening staffing, weekly ops readiness meetings, Local Evaluation Testing participation).
  • Serve as point of contact for CPMP measurement and Federal augmentation coordination if staffing shortfalls occur.
  • Be onboarded and available as soon as possible after the start of the task order transition period, and remain available throughout the transition period

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7 years of general management experience, OR at least 3 years as a certified Supervisory Transportation Security Officer (STSO) or higher position.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Aviation Management, Public Administration, Security Management, or a related discipline preferred; 4 years of directly related experience is acceptable in lieu of degree.
  • Any ONE of the following:
    • (a) formal certification in program/project management issued by the Federal Government (e.g., FAC-PM, DAWIA, U.S. DHS) or a non-government credential such as PMP; OR
    • (b) at least 5 years of management experience in aviation security, airport operations, or personnel security services (demonstrated supervisory experience in a Federal Government environment is highly desired).
  • Ability to communicate verbally and in writing in an effective, efficient, and professional manner.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance; TSA will sponsor the Facility/Personnel Security Clearance process.
  • U.S. citizenship required (a Secret clearance requires U.S. citizenship as a matter of federal policy).
  • Strong understanding of federal contract compliance, performance-based contracts (FFP), and operational metrics/CPMP-style measurement.
  • Excellent written/oral communication skills, with demonstrated experience briefing senior government customers (CO/FSD-level).
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including early/late coverage and 24/7 on-call availability, given ROC's extended screening hours

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior experience with the TSA Screening Partnership Program (SPP) or a comparable DHS/TSA aviation-security services contract.
  • Experience supporting TSA, DHS, FAA, or other federal aviation/homeland security programs.
  • Experience leading large operational transitions or workforce mobilizations.
  • Experience with DHS 4300A/NIST 800-53 compliance environments or comparable federal IT/cyber compliance oversight.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
  • Experience with workforce management systems, operational reporting tools, and performance dashboards.

Clearance/Vetting:

  • Secret security clearance required. TSA sponsors the Facility Security Clearance (FCL); a DD Form 254 must be incorporated into the contract before a Personnel Security Clearance (PCL) may be sought. Clearance must be maintained throughout the life of the contract - loss of, or inability to obtain, clearance may result in removal from the contract.
  • Separately and in addition to the Secret clearance, pre-hire vetting/suitability determination (Entry-on-Duty initiation through TSA Personnel Security) is also required, as it is for all Contractor personnel.

title: Cardiac Critical Care Faculty
description:
Overview:


The Heart Center at Nationwide Children's Hospital (NCH) seeks two Cardiac Intensivists, at any academic rank, to join its growing and dynamic program.

Candidates must have completed fellowship training in pediatric cardiology and/or critical care that included advanced cardiac intensive care training. Preference will be given to those who are boarded in pediatric cardiology and interested in an academic center with research and leadership opportunities for the candidate’s professional growth.

The successful applicant will join a group of ten multi-background academic cardiac intensivists and twelve dedicated nurse practitioners devoted to the CTICU, providing 24/7 in house coverage. Our free-standing CTICU is a 20-bed unit with 600+ admissions per year (medical and surgical). The Heart Center’s comprehensive services include hybrid palliation, comprehensive single ventricle program, thoracic organ transplantation, blood conservation strategies, and cardiac mechanical support. Current annual clinical metrics include: over 450 cardiothoracic surgeries, over 600 cardiac catheterizations and EP procedures, and over 24,000 cardiology outpatient visits. We have a pediatric and pediatric/adult combined cardiology fellowship programs.

The Heart Center embraces a culture of patient safety and quality, transparency, value-based care, public health awareness, excellence in education and engagement in translational/outcomes research. Our program is closely partnered with the Center for Cardiovascular Research at the NCH-Research Institute which provides infrastructure to support the clinical research enterprise. Research opportunities include engaging in basic science research, clinical research, translational research, population-based studies, and research-based education or quality improvement initiatives.

The Heart Center is also part of the Congenital Heart Collaborative between the University Rainbow Babies & Children’s Hospital (Cleveland, OH) and Nationwide Children’s Hospital heart programs which provides additional opportunity for collaborative research.

Job Description:

The Army Watercraft Systems Senior Analyst / Engineer provides technical repair, life-cycle sustainment, modernization, and technical management support for Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) shipboard electronic and electrical systems aboard U.S. Army vessels, ensuring mission readiness, regulatory compliance, and lifecycle sustainment of communications and navigation systems. This role is a subject matter expert on shipboard systems including Integrated Bridge Systems, Radar, Electronic Chart Display and Information Systems (ECDIS), and Global Maritime Distress Systems (GMDSS). As the Senior Analyst / Engineer, you will be a key member of the GDIT team supporting worldwide field sustainment operations for the U.S. Army Watercraft Program, reporting to the Watercraft C5ISR Sustainment Lead Engineer.


How the Army Watercraft Systems Senior Analyst / Engineer will make an impact:

  • Serve as a Senior Systems Analyst / Engineer providing worldwide field sustainment support for the U.S. Army Watercraft Program, including repair, modernization, and technical management of Army Watercraft Systems operating worldwide.
  • Perform technical repair and Life Cycle Support (LCS) for C5ISR marine systems in compliance with U.S. Military, U.S. Government agency, and Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications and regulations.
  • Test, maintain, and repair C5ISR systems as directed by senior personnel or as specified in formal training.
  • Apply experience with multimeters, amp meters, RF power meters, oscilloscopes, power generators, spectrum analyzers, and communication system analyzers.
  • Contribute to design discussions and lead and train less-experienced teammates within the team or technical area.
  • Analyze technical drawings, manuals, electronic schematics, and design documentation to troubleshoot, repair, and maintain electronic components and mechanical systems.
  • Set up, configure, and troubleshoot computer systems used for Radar and Electronic Chart Display Information Systems (ECDIS) and associated hardware/software components.
  • Install firmware, application software, software patches, and required firmware updates.
  • Develop and submit incident reports to senior personnel for C5ISR sustainment repair, system modernization tasks, preventive maintenance, and government special project activities.
  • Service shipboard power distribution and signal processing hardware.
  • Assist senior personnel with acoustic transducer replacement and interfacing for depth and speed monitoring systems.
  • Perform system installations, cable routing, shielding, and grounding protocols per senior guidance and vessel configuration drawings.
  • Conduct retrofit and modernization projects supporting vessel mission upgrades in accordance with regulatory compliance.
  • Install, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain Integrated Bridge Systems (IBS), Navigation Systems, Communication Systems, and Global Maritime Distress Safety Systems (GMDSS).
  • Conduct maintenance operations at the CECOM C5I Maintenance Support Facility Annex and Integrated Lab and Training Facility.
  • Support up to 50% worldwide travel in support of operational missions.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO SUCCEED


Bring your technical expertise and drive for innovation to GDIT. The Army Watercraft Systems Senior Analyst / Engineer must have:


  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, or a related discipline (or equivalent combination of education, technical training, and experience)
  • Experience: 8+ years of experience in U.S. Army Watercraft Systems marine electronic sustainment repair; or, in lieu of a degree, a minimum of 10 years of combined military and marine electronic systems repair experience on C5ISR electronic systems
  • Technical skills: Experience supporting U.S. Army Watercraft Systems (AWS) modernization, maintenance, and repair projects for the vessel's Integrated Bridge System (IBS), Navigation Systems, Tactical and Commercial Communication Systems, IFF Transponder System, and Global Maritime Distress Safety Systems (GMDSS) per Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) regulations; working knowledge of electrical distribution systems, power converters, power regulators, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), and shipboard cabling standards; strong troubleshooting, systems integration, maintenance management, and configuration control experience; ability to interpret and ensure compliance with technical configuration drawings, government agency regulations, and manufacturer/military technical documentation

description:

The Technical Writer and Trainer is accountable for documenting, standardizing, and enabling adoption of project delivery processes, tools, and governance, with a primary focus on the Project Management Best Practice Playbook, associated work instructions and the project management software. The role ensures that processes are clear, consistent, current, and usable, and that teams are effectively trained to apply them across the full project lifecycle.

KEY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Project Delivery Process Documentation & Standards

  • Develop, maintain and govern process documentation, including:
    • Project Management Best Practice Playbook content
    • Phase/Stage Gate requirements
    • Work Instructions (WIs), SOPs, and job aids
    • Standard forms, templates, and checklists
  • Translate complex delivery, controls, and governance requirements into clear, concise, and practical guidance for project practitioners.
  • Ensure alignment between documented processes and:
    • Project Management Office (PMO) & Project Controls Office (PCO) governance
    • Quality frameworks (Quality Assurance (QA), Non-Conformance Reporting (NCR), stage gate controls)
    • Client-specific delivery requirements where applicable
  • Actively manage version control, publish updates, and retire obsolete documentation.

Project Management Software Enablement & Documentation

  • Serve as the primary author and curator of software related documentation, including:
    • End-to-end lifecycle guides
    • Role-based guides (PM, PC, PCO, Directors)
    • Module-specific instructions (forms, correspondence, cost management, schedules, close-out, reporting)
  • Ensure software documentation reinforces:
    • Data integrity standards
    • Required fields and workflows
    • Alignment with project delivery stage/phase gates and charters
  • Work closely with software configuration, PCO, and PMO teams to keep documentation synchronized with system changes and enhancements.

Training Design & Delivery

  • Design and deliver structured project delivery process and supporting software training programs, including:
    • Onboarding training for new hires
    • Refresher and role-based training for existing staff
    • Targeted training for process or system changes
  • Develop training materials such as:
    • Slide decks and facilitator guides
    • Self-serve learning content using video technology,
    • Quizzes, job aids, and knowledge checks
  • Support account-specific or program-specific training rollouts as required.

Adoption, Quality & Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with PCO, PMO, and PDS Leadership to:
    • Identify gaps in process understanding or execution
    • Target training and documentation to address risk areas
  • Incorporate feedback from:
    • Training sessions
    • Audits, NCRs, and QA reviews
    • PMWeb data quality issues
  • Use lessons learned to continuously improve clarity, usability, and effectiveness of documentation and training.

Governance & Stakeholder Integration

  • Act as a bridge between strategy, governance, and execution, ensuring that:
    • Leadership expectations are clearly translated into operational guidance
    • Teams understand “what good looks like” and how it is measured
  • Collaborate with:
    • PDS Leadership
    • PMO / PCO
    • Software configuration and support teams
    • Quality, Risk, and Controls lead(s)
  • Support enterprise initiatives related to standardization, digitization, and delivery maturity.

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS

  • Strong technical writing and instructional design capability.
  • Deep understanding of project delivery, controls, and governance in a PMO/PCO environment.
  • Practical experience translating complex workflows into clear user guidance.
  • Comfortable working across operations, technology, and leadership teams.

  • Advanced Knowledge of MS Project, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio, project management and video creation software.
  • Strong interpersonal, and communication skills.
  • Organizational skills with the ability to handle multiple concurrent activities and to work successfully under pressure.
  • Ability to manage priorities while taking direction from several managers and communicate effectively to manage workload and expectations.

title: Software Engineer
description:
About the Role

We're hiring a new-graduate Software Systems Design Engineer focused on blockchain security and protocol design. You'll work at the intersection of cryptography, distributed systems, and adversarial security — redesigning and hardening wallet and core systems against protocol- and architecture-level threats. This is a builder's role for someone who thinks like an attacker and designs like an engineer.

Protocol Analysis & Design
  • Analyze and evaluate how mainstream blockchain protocols work under the hood (Ethereum/EVM, Cosmos SDK, Substrate, Solana, etc.), and redesign wallet systems grounded in secure cryptographic mechanisms.
  • Develop hardening and mitigation plans for the wallet system against known protocol-level vulnerabilities and emerging risks.
System Security Re-architecture & Hardening
  • Drive security-requirement-driven re-architecture and maintenance of existing software systems.
  • Embed security assumptions at the architecture level, designing and implementing defense-in-depth for critical modules to reduce single points of failure and ambiguous trust boundaries.
Research, Audit & Response
  • Track cutting-edge blockchain attack techniques and defenses, and turn research into shippable system improvements.
  • Participate in or lead security audits of internal systems and open-source dependencies, driving remediation and architectural improvements.
Background & Experience
  • Master's degree or above preferred in Computer Science, Cryptography, or Network/Cyber Security.
  • New graduate or up to 2 years of work experience.
Core Technical Skills
  • Development & architecture: Strong command of at least one systems-programming language among Java / Go / Rust / C++. Proficient in distributed systems design, concurrency models, and performance optimization.
  • Security domain knowledge: Familiar with threat modeling, secure coding standards, penetration-testing mindset, and supply-chain security.
Key Soft Skills
  • Security mindset & risk thinking: Operates on a \"zero trust\" principle by default and reasons systematically about attack surfaces.
  • Analysis & abstraction: Translates complex, ambiguous security requirements into clear, verifiable technical architecture and module designs.
  • Engineering craft & influence: Builds a security culture across the team through design docs, code reviews, and tech talks.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Deep understanding of the full technical stack of at least one mainstream blockchain (networking, consensus, execution, storage). Strong grasp of smart contract security and common vulnerability patterns.
  • Practical command of how public-key cryptography, hash functions, zero-knowledge proofs, and threshold signatures apply — and where their risks lie — in real systems.

title: Freight Handler Part-Time
description:
Starting rate of pay $20.16/ hour
Shift times: 1600-2000

POSITION OVERVIEW:

Transport freight across dock area to/from trailers for loading to trailers.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Perform freight handling using appropriate motorized and manual equipment, including but not limited to: forklift, pallet jack and hand truck.

  • Verify documentation matches freight description (e.g. type, weight, hazardous materials), using current electronic or manual system.

  • Secure freight inside trailers using appropriate tools and supplies (e.g. pallets, straps, rope).

  • Recoup/repair damaged freight when necessary.

  • Verify and complete required documentation and reports.

  • Assist customers with freight and freight documentation as needed.

  • Perform hostling duties if required.

  • Comply with all applicable laws/regulations, as well as company policies/procedures.

  • Perform other duties as required.

DISCLAIMER: This job description is general in nature and is not designed to contain or to be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, essential functions and qualifications required of employees assigned to the job.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred.

  • Must be at least 18 years of age.

  • Prior experience in warehousing, freight handling and/or fork lift operations preferred.

  • If hostler/yard mule duties required, experience preferred.

  • Ability to count and perform basic math, with or without a calculator.

  • Basic written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to lift/carry hand freight of varying weights several times a week, to lift dock plates weighing approximately 100 pounds, and to open trailer doors requiring approximately 75 pounds of lift force, up to several times per day or more.

  • Ability to bend, twist, squat, pushing/pulling freight throughout shift.

  • Ability to work independently and/or as a team member.

  • Previous dock/warehouse experience preferred.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • Dock environment; exposure to varied weather conditions, exhaust, fumes, dust, noise.

  • Hours may vary due to operational need.

  • Frequent contact with service center personnel; fast-paced, deadline oriented.
