If you are a current associate, you will need to apply through our internal career site. Please log into Workday and click on the Jobs Hub app or search for Browse Jobs.

CLIENT SERVICE COORDINATOR

This posting will remain open for a minimum of two weeks from the posting date.

A career at Banfield means you'll find yourself working in the pet healthcare field alongside industry experts with a chance to make a difference in the lives of pets and the clients we serve through client education and effective communication. Work in a fun team environment that offers a clear career path you can pursue if continued growth and learning is your goal.

JOB SUMMARY

The Client Service Coordinator ("CSC") drives the flow of clients and pets through the hospital, maximizes the productivity of the veterinary medical team (in terms of numbers of clients and pets), ensures good communication with associates and clients, and coordinates the care of clients and pets in a happy, welcoming, friendly and efficient manner, influencing clients to return and refer their friends and families.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS

  • Live and exemplify the Five Principles of Mars, Inc. within self and team.

  • Actively recruit new clients by promoting hospital services and route the flow of clients and pets to ensure superior client care and maximum productivity of the veterinary medical team.

  • Maximize the number of pets seen by the hospital team through a productive and efficiently run hospital to support the needs of our wellness plan clients.

  • Provide professional, efficient and exceptional service at all times. This includes encouraging hospital visits, welcoming clients and pets, ensuring that they are comfortable in the hospital, and educating them about their pet's health.

  • Educate clients about Optimum Wellness Plans, preventative care, pet health needs and hospital services

  • Assist incoming clients by completing the required documentation, entering all pet information and history in the computer, utilizing proper collars and tags for identification, and ensuring prompt service.

  • Assist outgoing clients by providing all necessary instructions, information and invoices, dispensing prescription items per the veterinarian's instructions, selling retail products and scheduling future appointments.

  • Manage the finances by maintaining accurate balances and utilizing proper opening and closing procedures.

  • Conduct administrative functions as necessary.

  • Other job duties as assigned.

THE FIVE PRINCIPLES

Every associate including the CSC has an important contribution to make to the veterinary team. We’re looking for CSCs who are dedicated to their work, have a positive attitude and use our Five Principles:

  • Quality – The consumer is our boss, quality is our work, and value for money is our goal.

  • Responsibility – As individuals, we demand total responsibility from ourselves; as associates, we support the responsibility of others.

  • Mutuality – A mutual benefit is a shared benefit; a shared benefit will endure.

  • Efficiency – We use resources to the full, waste nothing and do only what we can do best.

  • Freedom – We need freedom to shape our future; we need profit to remain free.

HIRING QUALIFICATIONS

Competencies

  • Leadership:

    • Integrity & Trust

    • Action Oriented

  • Functional

    • Communication Skills

    • Client Service Skills

    • Priority Setting

    • Time Management

  • Capabilities and Experience (can do)

    • Ability to multi-task- Manages multiple tasks at one time; quickly and accurately shifts attention among multiple tasks under distracting conditions without loss of accuracy or appearance of frustration.

    • Communication skills - Reads, writes and speaks fluent English, using appropriate grammar, style and vocabulary. Correctly spells commonly used English words and job specific terms. Demonstrates exceptionally strong written and verbal communication skills.

    • Organizational ability – Demonstrates a systematic approach in carrying out assignments. Is very orderly and excels at cutting through confusion and turning chaos into order.

    • Problem solving skills - Demonstrates a strong ability to identify, analyze and solve problems. Translates problems into practical solutions.

    • Client service skills - Consistently ensures the team provides the client with attentive, courteous and informative service. Gains and shows personal satisfaction from delivering great service.

    • Intellectual ability - Accurately and consistently follows instructions delivered in an oral, written or diagram format. Can provide directions.

    • Mathematical ability - Ability to add, subtract, multiply and divide, and to compute rate, ratio and percent; ability to convert units of measurement.

    • Computer skills - Comfortably and confidently uses a computer and specialized software. Microsoft Word, Excel, Access, Outlook, etc.

  • Attitudes (will do)

    • Initiative – shows willingness and aptitude to use own discretion in taking appropriate steps in finding solutions to problems; presents options and ideas to enhance current processes or procedures. Takes on additional responsibility when both big and small tasks need to be done.

    • Integrity – Firmly adheres to the values and ethics of Banfield Pet Hospitals. Exhibits honesty, discretion, and sound judgment.

    • Cooperativeness – Willing to work with others, collaborating and compromising where necessary; promptly share relevant information with others.

    • Flexibility – Is open to changing situations and opportunities and is willing to perform all tasks assigned.

    • Independence – Able and willing to perform tasks and duties without supervision.

    • Tolerance for Stress / Resiliency – Maintains a positive “can do” outlook, rebounds quickly from frustrations and unpleasantness, and maintains composure and friendly demeanor while dealing with stressful situations.

  • Special Working Conditions

    • Ability to work at a computer for long periods of time.

    • Ability to be confident around pets (i.e., dogs, cats, birds, reptiles, etc.)

    • Client needs and work volume may often require more than 40 hours per week to complete essential duties of this job. This position requires special hours including working weekends and evenings.

    • Must have mental processes for reasoning, remembering, mathematics and language ability (reading, writing, and speaking the English language) to perform the duties proficiently.

    • The noise level in the work environment is moderately high.

    • Requires sufficient ambulatory skills in order to perform duties while at hospital.

    • Ability to stand, walk, stoop, kneel, crouch, and climb as well as manipulate (lift, carry, move) up to 50 pounds.

    • Requires good hand-eye coordination, arm-hand-finger dexterity with the ability to grasp, and visual acuity to use a keyboard and operate equipment.

    • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

    • Associate is routinely exposed to a variety of pets that may bite or scratch, and on occasion, exposed to anesthesia, radiation, biological hazards and medication/controlled substances.

  • Experience, Education and/or Training

    • High School Diploma or equivalent preferred.

    • Must be at least 18 years old to perform duties involving radiography (x-ray) and exposure to radioactive substances.

    • One year of related experience required with customer service preferred.

    • Medical background (veterinary technician, human healthcare, pharmaceutical, etc.) with medical terminology training is preferred.

title: Data Engineer, Senior
description:
Data Engineer, Senior

The Opportunity:

Ever-expanding technology like IoT, machine learning, and artificial intelligence means that there’s more structured and unstructured data available today than ever before. As a data engineer, you know that organizing data can yield pivotal insights when it’s gathered from disparate sources. We need an experienced data engineer like you to help our clients find answers in their data to impact important missions, from fraud detection to cancer research, to national intelligence.


As a Data Engineer at Booz Allen, you’ll help build advanced technology solutions and implement data engineering activities on some of the most mission-driven projects in the industry. You’ll deploy and develop pipelines and platforms that organize and make disparate data meaningful.


Here, you’ll work with and guide a multi-disciplinary team of analysts, data engineers, developers, and data consumers in a fast-paced, agile environment. You’ll use your experience in analytical exploration and data examination while you manage the assessment, design, building, and maintenance of scalable platforms for your clients.


Join us. The world can’t wait.


You Have:

  • 10+ years of experience designing data warehouse or data lake, RESTful API models, event processing, or business intelligence for software systems
  • Experience building scalable ETL or ELT data pipelines, automating large-scale batch and streaming data workflows, and parsing structured, unstructured, or event-streaming data
  • Experience with coding in software programming languages, including Postgres, SQL, Python, Scala, Spark, or Java
  • Experience using Apache Spark, Apache NiFi, or Databricks
  • Experience performing tuning on data lake architecture to optimize cloud storage and pipeline performance
  • Experience with data management solutions that address aspects of data catalog, data usage, governance policies, and lifecycle management
  • Top Secret clearance

  • Experience using and developing data systems with AWS and Microsoft Azure cloud data products such as AWS EMR, AWS Glue, Azure Dataverse, Azure Data Factory, and Power Apps

  • Experience with federal information system policies, including NIST 800.53 and FISMA, data security, access controls, and data protection techniques
  • Experience creating and improving continuous automation across multiple technical stacks, and automating CD/CD pipelines with tools such as Jenkins or GitHub

title: AI Solutions Analyst
description:
Public Consulting Group LLC (PCG) is a leading public sector solutions implementation and operations improvement firm that partners with health, education, and human services agencies to improve lives. Founded in 1986, PCG employs approximately 2,000 professionals throughout the U.S.—all committed to delivering solutions that change lives for the better. The firm is a member of a family of companies with experience in all 50 states, and clients in three Canadian provinces and Europe. PCG offers clients a multidisciplinary approach to meet challenges, pursue opportunities, and serve constituents across the public sector. To learn more, visit .

PCG is seeking an AI Solutions Analyst to support the design, delivery, and ongoing monitoring of AI-enabled solutions within state government environments. This role bridges client-facing requirements work with hands-on responsibility for how the AI system actually performs — translating policy and program needs into structured requirements, and using evaluation data to diagnose and improve system output quality.

The ideal candidate combines business analysis discipline with practical, hands-on fluency in enterprise AI — not just understanding how agentic workflows behave, but analyzing evaluation results with basic statistical reasoning and using that diagnosis to shape system behavior, within real-world constraints of performance, cost, and explainability.

This role is ideal for candidates who want to work inside how enterprise AI environments by writing the requirements, measuring the results, and closing the gap between the two.

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a data science or ML infrastructure role (no model architecture, training pipelines, or platform engineering)
  • Not a traditional business analyst role focused only on documentation
  • Not a project manager role only owning delivery execution or sprint ceremonies
  • Not a prompt-only or AI tool usage role without enterprise context understanding
  • Not a role where success is measured by prompt-writing volume — tuning here is diagnosis-led, grounded in evaluation data, not trial-and-error prompting

Key Responsibilities

Client Engagement & Requirements Facilitation

  • Support and lead client requirements sessions and discovery discussions
  • Translate policy and operational workflows into structured requirements
  • Serve as a bridge between stakeholders and technical teams

AI Solution Design & Tuning

  • Support design of AI-enabled solutions and define use cases
  • Develop and document AI workflows
  • Design evaluation test sets with attention to sample size and representativeness across case types (LTC, ADB, etc.)
  • Analyze evaluation results using basic statistical reasoning — error rates, false positive/negative patterns, distribution of failure modes — to identify where and why the system underperforms
  • Iterate on prompts and instructions to address root causes identified through evaluation analysis
  • Identify tradeoffs related to performance, cost, token usage, and explainability
  • Partner with technical leads on tuning cycles within established review and sign-off processes

Delivery & Operations Support

  • Support broader program operations as needed — process design, cross-workstream coordination, and other work that helps scale delivery beyond a single engagement

Required Qualifications

  • Strong communication skills
  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
  • 4+ years of experience as a Business Analyst, Solutions Analyst, or Consultant
  • Experience translating complex needs into structured deliverables
  • Client-facing experience in requirements sessions and workshops
  • Working knowledge of basic statistics — sample sizes, error rates, false positive/negative distinction, and comfort reading distributions — sufficient to design representative evaluation test sets and interpret results
  • Hands-on experience iterating on prompts/instructions for LLM-based systems in a production or near-production setting
  • Working knowledge of AI systems, including behavior, limitations, and agentic workflows
  • Practical understanding of model selection tradeoffs, context/cost constraints, and agentic workflow limitations beyond prompt-level interaction with frontier models
  • Technical understanding of system architecture, data flows, APIs, and integrations

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting public-sector or compliance-driven programs
  • Familiarity with AI implementation patterns such as RAG and multi-agent workflows
  • Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS Bedrock preferred, Azure acceptable)

title: Analyst/Strategist II - Grant Management Office
description:
Overview

The national offices of the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.), A Corporation (“A Corp”) “PC(USA)”, based in Louisville Kentucky, serve with mid-councils, congregations, worshipping communities, and partner organizations to carry forth the mission of Jesus Christ. Approximately 400 individuals, diverse in race, age, gender, sexual orientation, faith, skills, and more, come together as colleagues to work for a world where justice reigns, peace prevails, and God’s love extends to all people. This community comprises the staff of national entities: the Presbyterian Life & Witness, the Presbyterian Publishing Corporation, Presbyterian Women, Investment and Loan Program, and the Administrative Services Group.

Basic Commitment: This position calls for a commitment to the mission of the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) as noted in its theological confessions, the Book of Order, and the actions of the General Assembly.

Position Summary

The Grant Management Office (GMO) Strategist/Analyst serves as the agency’s lead for grant reporting, impact analysis, and grant Review (selection) design and management within the AkoyaGo Grant Management System (GMS). This role ensures that grant decisions and outcomes are transparent, equitable, data‑informed, and aligned with Presbyterian Life & Witness (PL&W) values and priorities.

By combining reporting and impact analysis with stewardship of the Review process, this position strengthens faithful use of restricted funds, supports consistent grantmaking practices across ministries, and equips leadership with actionable insights to guide mission‑driven decisions.

Primary Responsibilities

1. Grant Review (Selection) Strategy & Management

Using AkoyaGo’s Review framework, the Strategist/Analyst will:

  • Partner with grant sponsors and program staff to:
    • Define review goals and selection methods aligned with program purpose and PL&W priorities
    • Determine appropriate review models (e.g., staff, peer, hybrid, panel)
  • Configure Review processes in AkoyaGo, including:
    • Reviewer assignments and access
    • Scoring criteria and weights
    • Review forms and interfaces used to record scores, recommendations, and observations
  • Recruit, onboard, and manage review teams, including:
    • Developing reviewer guidance and expectations
    • Coordinating timelines and communication
    • Monitoring progress and addressing bottlenecks or concerns
  • Evaluate Review outcomes and methodologies to:
    • Assess equity, consistency, and effectiveness
    • Identify bias, misalignment, or unintended barriers
    • Recommend improvements to strengthen future grant cycles

2. Grant Reporting & Impact Analysis

The Strategist/Analyst will lead enterprise‑level reporting by:

  • Designing and maintaining standardized grant reports that support:
    • Leadership decision‑making
    • Program evaluation and learning
    • Accountability and stewardship of restricted funds
  • Analyzing grant data across programs to:
    • Identify trends, outcomes, gaps, and emerging needs
    • Support assessment of alignment with PL&W mission priorities
  • Ensuring reporting standards and definitions are applied consistently across programs
  • Partnering with Communications, Development, and program staff to translate data into meaningful narratives about grant impact

3. System Stewardship & Data Integrity

This role supports sustainable use of the GMS by:

  • Maintaining consistent configuration standards for Review and reporting
  • Supporting data quality, validation, and documentation practices
  • Identifying system improvements and workflow refinements
  • Partnering with IT, Finance, and Legal as needed to support integrations and compliance

4. Training & Support

The Strategist/Analyst will:

  • Develop and deliver training for:
    • Grant administrators
    • Reviewers
    • Program and mission staff
  • Provide ongoing consultation and troubleshooting support
  • Create user‑friendly documentation and guidance materials

Scope & Impact

This role influences how millions of dollars in mission‑critical grants are selected, evaluated, and reported. By shaping Review processes and impact reporting, the Strategist/Analyst directly supports equity, transparency, and faithful stewardship—core commitments of Presbyterian Life & Witness.

Training Plan

Grant Management Office Strategist/Analyst

This training plan balances system skills, grantmaking practice, and PL&W mission alignment.

Phase 1: Foundations (First 30–45 Days)

Grant & Mission Context

  • PL&W vision, priorities, and grantmaking principles
  • Overview of Grants Centralization goals and GMO role
  • Understanding restricted funds and stewardship responsibilities

System Orientation (AkoyaGo)

  • GMS structure, terminology, and workflows
  • Distinction between application, Review, award, and reporting phases
  • Data standards and core configuration principles

Phase 2: Review (Selection) Management (Days 45–90)

AkoyaGo Review Configuration

  • Designing Review workflows
  • Building scoring rubrics and weighted criteria
  • Creating reviewer interfaces and guidance materials

Reviewer Management

  • Recruiting and onboarding review teams
  • Establishing expectations and timelines
  • Managing conflicts of interest and accessibility needs

Equity‑Centered Review Practices

  • Identifying bias in criteria and scoring
  • Aligning Review design with PL&W values
  • Evaluating outcomes for fairness and consistency

title: System Integration Engineer
description:
Join a team that is helping modernize the future of air traffic management while supporting one of the nation's most critical transportation missions. Leidos is seeking a Systems Integration Engineer to join the Terminal Flight Data Manager (TFDM) program supporting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). In this role, you will be responsible for integrating, validating, and deploying mission-critical capabilities that improve the safety, efficiency, and reliability of the National Airspace System (NAS).


TFDM is the FAA's NextGen surface management solution that enhances airport surface and terminal airspace operations through an integrated traffic control and management system. As part of this team, you'll collaborate with software engineers, system engineers, and FAA stakeholders to deliver capabilities that directly support air traffic controllers and airport operations across the country.


This position offers more than a traditional integration and test role. You'll have the opportunity to work directly with FAA customers during system deployments, formal test events, and customer acceptance activities at airports nationwide. You'll see your work transition from the lab into live operational environments while helping deliver technology that supports one of the world's most complex aviation systems.


Location: This position is based in our Egg Harbor, NJ office with a hybrid schedule of three days per week in the office and two days working remotely.

Travel: Up to 50% travel is required and is a key part of this role. You'll travel to FAA airport locations throughout the United States to support system integration, customer demonstrations, formal testing, and operational deployments. Working alongside FAA personnel in live airport environments provides a unique opportunity to gain firsthand operational experience, build strong customer relationships, and see the direct impact of your work as TFDM is deployed across the National Airspace System. Travel is typically one to two weeks per trip.


Applicants selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information.


Primary Responsibilities

As a member of a highly collaborative engineering team, you will:

  • Integrate, configure, and validate TFDM capabilities within both physical and virtual integration laboratories.
  • Execute system integration, verification, and validation activities to ensure the system is properly configured and operating within the National Airspace System.
  • Support formal customer demonstrations, verification events, and customer acceptance testing with FAA stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with software, systems engineering, networking, and infrastructure teams to investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve complex system-level issues.
  • Analyze integration and test results, identify root causes, and provide detailed technical documentation supporting issue resolution.
  • Support deployment and integration activities at FAA operational facilities, including Air Traffic Control Towers (ATCTs).
  • Execute system interface testing and validate communications across internal and external NAS interfaces.
  • Coordinate integration activities with FAA personnel and cross-functional Leidos engineering teams.
  • Develop automated tools, scripts, and AI-assisted solutions that improve testing efficiency, reduce manual effort, and streamline repetitive tasks.
  • Support remote deployment activities by coordinating with infrastructure, networking, and installation teams.
  • Learn and maintain a deep understanding of TFDM architecture, system functionality, interfaces, and operational workflows.
  • Partner with Systems Engineering to develop integration and test strategies for new capabilities and system enhancements.
  • Integrate services with databases, messaging systems, and external APIs.
  • Troubleshoot XML messaging, JMS queue configurations, networking issues, IP configurations, and interface connectivity.
  • Demonstrate system capabilities during formal "run-for-record" events supporting customer acceptance and release readiness.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentoring to junior integration engineers while helping ensure program milestones are successfully achieved.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline. Equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Ability to obtain an FAA SF-85P Public Trust.
  • Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with engineers, program leadership, and FAA customers.
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% to support customer deployments and operational testing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating mission-critical or highly available systems.
  • FAA or Air Traffic Management domain experience.
  • Knowledge of National Airspace System (NAS) interfaces including FDIO, STARS, TBFM, and ASDE-X.
  • Experience leading formal integration, verification, or customer acceptance events.
  • Familiarity with Agile development methodologies including Scrum or Kanban.
  • Understanding of systems engineering processes including requirements management, interface definition, and verification.
  • Experience working with distributed systems, enterprise messaging, and service-oriented architectures.

title: Inventory Cycle Counter - Stellar Manufacturing
description:
DIVE IN TO A NEW CAREER WITH A LESLIE'S COMPANY:

In September 2022, Stellar Manufacturing was acquired by Leslie's as an affiliate. Stellar Manufacturing is a contract manufacturer of solid particle products and specializes in chemical processing services such as specialty tableting, compaction granulation, and granular filling. We support the manufacturing of a variety of consumer and industrial products including water treatment chemicals, janitorial and sanitation products, agrochemicals, raw materials, and more. With over 30 years of providing best-in-class products and solutions to our customers, there is nothing that we value more than the development and growth of our team. Both Leslie's and Stellar strive to create a positive and fun atmosphere where our Team Members feel valued and are enthusiastic about the contributions they make to the success of Stellar.

Job Overview:
The Inventory Cycle Counter is responsible for maintaining accurate inventory records by performing daily cycle counts, investigating discrepancies, and ensuring the proper movement and documentation of raw materials, components, and finished goods. This position supports manufacturing operations by monitoring inventory levels, identifying replenishment needs, and maintaining accurate inventory transactions. The role works closely with manufacturing, supply chain, and management to improve inventory accuracy, streamline material handling processes, and support continuous improvement initiatives.

Compensation Range: $25.00 - $28.00 /Hourly

Compensation within range to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge and skills, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform daily cycle counts of raw materials, components, and finished goods to maintain inventory accuracy and support production needs.
  • Monitor and communicate the receipt, movement, and disbursement of materials and finished goods.
  • Record inventory movements and transactions in the Inventory Control System (ICS).
  • Monitor inventory levels, identify depleted items or materials reaching reorder points, and place replenishment orders as needed.
  • Identify, investigate, and report discrepancies between physical inventory counts and system records.
  • Analyze inventory discrepancies, determine potential causes, and communicate findings to the supervisor.
  • Assist in planning and conducting periodic physical inventories.
  • Prepare inventory reports and analyze data to support management decisions.
  • Load, unload, and organize materials on pallets, trays, racks, and shelves to facilitate accurate inventory counts.
  • Count, weigh, and record materials received, moved, or handled.
  • Safely transport materials using manual handling equipment, pallet jacks, and forklifts.
  • Maintain forklift cleanliness and ensure equipment is properly charged and ready for use.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment, promptly reporting unsafe conditions to the supervisor.
  • Follow plant labeling requirements and ensure chemicals are properly labeled, stored, and handled.
  • Identify and recommend improvements to material handling processes and procedures.
  • Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of standardized inventory control processes and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
  • Ensure inventory control activities align with established quality management standards and company procedures.
  • Assist in documenting customer complaints and nonconformance reports (NCAPs), as applicable.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, and quality assurance teams to address inventory-related concerns and support process improvements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve inventory accuracy, operational efficiency, and overall process consistency.
  • Partner with cross-functional departments to identify inventory challenges, develop performance measurements, and implement continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Assist in creating, updating, and maintaining departmental standard operating procedures.
  • Communicate inventory findings, material shortages, and operational concerns to appropriate departments and management.
    Perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualification:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • 1–3 years of experience in a manufacturing environment preferred.
  • 1–3 years of inventory control, cycle counting, or related warehouse experience preferred.
  • Experience operating standing and seated forklifts.
  • Experience using inventory management systems preferred.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate inventory records.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to investigate inventory discrepancies and communicate findings effectively.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to safely lift, carry, or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Flexibility and willingness to adapt to changing priorities and operational needs.
  • Commitment to workplace safety, quality standards, and continuous improvement.

We offer our employees competitive compensation, extensive paid training, comprehensive and flexible suite of benefits package, 401K with company match, team member discounts, rewards for top performers, and most importantly career advancement opportunities.

title: Graphics Artist, Journeyman
description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?


At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. Your greatest work is ahead!


The Intelligence Sector seeks highly qualified and trained Journeyman-level Graphics Artists to support United States Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM) operations through production of high-quality and high-visibility graphics underpinning critical visual communications to include briefings, documents, and web materials. As part of a collaborative team, candidates will conceptualize, design, and deliver visually compelling products that effectively communicate complex information in a professional, clear, and aesthetically pleasing manner.


This opportunity is in anticipation of a potential future contract award.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Provide timely, accurate, relevant support in manner that best supports USCYBERCOM as graphics artist supporting multiple customers across the USCYERCOM J3, Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF), and Joint Task Force-ARES (JTF-ARES).
  • Design and produce high-quality graphic content using Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative Suite products.
  • Develop visual concepts from start to finish with creativity and precision, while adhering to USCYBERCOM branding and presentation standards.
  • Collaborate with technical SMEs and leaders to transform complex information into clean, engaging visual content.

  • Design materials for internal and external communications, including documents, infographics, presentations, and web-based assets.
  • Contribute to the development of analytic standards and best practices, continuously improving methodologies and products.
  • Ensure compliance with DoD and USCYBERCOM policies, regulations, and frameworks, and interpret and apply laws, regulations, and any other applicable guidance relevant to daily activities.
  • Communicate complex information, concepts, or ideas in a confident and well-organized manner through verbal, written, and/or visual means.

What does Leidos need from me?

  • Top Secret/SCI (TS/SCI) security clearance with Polygraph, upon Application, to be consideration for this position.
  • Associate’s degree or higher in Graphic Design, Visual Communications, Multimedia Arts, or related field. Additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  • Three to Five plus years’ experience in graphic design within a professional environment, with preference for previous experience supporting DoD or Intelligence Community (IC) organizations.
  • Ability to provide support timely, accurate, relevant graphics artist support to analytical production, to include documents, summaries, issue papers, talking points, and briefings.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft 365 and Adobe Creative Suite.
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating a range of graphic design skills, especially in presentation graphics and executive-level content.
  • Knowledge of computer networking fundamentals as well as concepts, terminology, and operations of a wide range of communications media (computer and telephone networks, satellite, fiber, wireless).
  • Demonstrated understanding of formatting for classified and unclassified briefing environments.
  • Strong attention to detail, ability to follow branding guidelines, and commitment to high visual standards.
  • Display excellent interpersonal and communication skills; ability to receive and apply feedback effectively.
  • Demonstrated proficiency working in a fast-paced collaborative environment, ability to proactively multi-task and meet short deadlines.

Favorable if you have:

  • Bachelors’ degree or higher within field of Graphic Design, Visual Communications, Multimedia Arts, or a related field.
  • Familiarity with USCYBERCOM organizational structure and mission.
  • Experience designing for executive-level or military audiences.
  • Prior experience providing graphic design support to Joint operations across multiple warfighting domains.
  • Demonstrated understanding of DoD and IC collaboration and graphics design best practices.
  • Desired Certifications: DoD 8570 IAT Level II (CCNA Security, COMPTIA CySA+, COMPTIA Security + CE, GICSP, GSEC, SSCP).

This posting is for multiple opportunities ranging in years of experience. Level of opportunity including compensation, will be matched to the candidate's experience.

title: SoC IP and System Applications
description:
About the role

TylSemi is looking for a IP and Systems Application Engineer who can sit at the intersection of silicon, IP, and customer success. You will own the operational thread that connects our stretagic initiatives to customers — making sure every engagement moves with precision from idea to silicon.

This is a high-visibility, high-ownership role at a company in its earliest and most consequential stage. You will work directly with founders, customers, the leading semiconductor ecosystem players. No layers, no ambiguity about impact.

What you'll do

  • Technical fluency in SoC or chiplet design flows — enough to understand RTL milestones, DV sign-off, PD handoffs, and silicon bring-up phases without needing translation
  • Strong communication skills — comfortable presenting program status and risk posture to internal and external stakeholders
  • Proficiency with program tracking tools (and spreadsheet-based trackers); experience building program infrastructure from scratch is a plus
  • Familiarity with key connectivity IPs UCIe, PCIe Gen 5/6/7+, or high-bandwidth D2D interconnect standards is a strong plus

Nice to Have to Shine

  • Prior experience at an IP company, chiplet startup, merchant silicon company, or systems company
  • Background in AI/ML infrastructure silicon — accelerators, network switches, CPO-enabled platforms
  • Exposure to EDA infrastructure programs (SNPS/CDNS cloud flows)

title: Human Physiology Systems Advisor
description:
Human Physiology Systems Advisor

The Opportunity:

To achieve an organization’s mission, leaders need strong team members who can create processes, communicate requirements, and develop innovative solutions throughout the execution of the mission. Whether completing an immediate task, recognizing a process gap, recommending a solution, or flexing to support an emerging requirement, our clients need someone who can help manage operations while managing responses to external inquiries in a timely manner. That is why we need an experienced Human Physiology Systems Advisor like you to provide technical expertise and project development for emerging opportunities within healthcare.

As part of our team, you'll serve as a strategic technical advisor to the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H), helping conceptualize, create, and execute advanced government-funded research and development (R&D) programs to accelerate better health outcomes for everyone. You’ll work with world-class scientists and engineers to support the development of high-impact solutions to society's most challenging health problems. You’ll leverage your technical expertise to provide strategic assessments of new technologies in support to senior ARPA-H decision-makers. You’ll maintain responsibility for producing and presenting findings and recommendations to a team of colleagues and clients on the feasibility and potential impact of future research programs, assisting with the management of current programs, and facilitating commercialization of successfully developed technologies.

You'll serve as a Human Physiology Systems Advisor, helping clients to develop stakeholder management strategies, establish new business processes, and complete research and analysis to determine viable solutions. You will be responsible for managing incoming requirements, facilitating engagements within offices and across the agency, and being readily available to shift your focus to fulfill emerging client requests. Your attention to detail, flexibility, communication skills, understanding of the client's mission, and problem-solving will enable the mission's success.

What You’ll Work On:

  • Provide technical and strategic support across a portfolio of programs related to tissue and organoid manufacturing, tissue and organ preservation, ex vivo organ perfusion and diagnostics, and other translational technologies relevant to tissue and organ recovery, preservation, and transplantation.
  • Evaluate technologies in the context of clinical and operational realities, including donor tissue and organ recovery, preservation logistics, perfusion-enabled assessment or intervention, and transplant-center workflow.
  • Conduct landscape analyses and technical diligence on emerging capabilities, vendors, performers, and scientific trends, and advise on the scientific plausibility, translational feasibility, manufacturability, and adoption potential of proposed approaches.
  • Provide insight into how innovations may intersect with the broader transplant ecosystem, including organ procurement organizations, transplant centers, and applicable federal regulators and stakeholders.
  • Maintain awareness of relevant scientific, clinical, regulatory, and market developments.
  • Review and assess technical proposals, performer submissions, milestones, deliverables, and program risks.
  • Provide feedback, organize reviewer comments, and draft recommendations, project summaries, and presentation materials.
  • Help identify subject matter experts, potential performers, test or evaluation partners, and transition stakeholders across academia, industry, clinical practice, and government environments.
  • Assist with program management functions, including preparing for technical meetings, conducting site visits, consolidating performer progress, identifying schedule risks, and creating briefing materials.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

  • Experience synthesizing complex scientific information into concise written and visual products for decision support
  • Experience in organ preservation, ex vivo organ perfusion and diagnostics, transplant biology, regenerative medicine, or translational bioengineering
  • Experience supporting complex R&D efforts involving academic, clinical, or industrial stakeholders
  • Ability to critically evaluate technical data, experimental plans, and development pathways
  • Ability to work across multidisciplinary teams
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time
  • Master’s degree in Physiology, Systems Biology, Bioengineering, Tissue Engineering, or Regenerative Medicine and 10+ years of experience in transplantation, organ preservation, transplant surgery, or transplant medicine, or Doctorate degree and 7+ years of experience in transplantation, organ preservation, transplant surgery, or transplant medicine

Nice If You Have:

  • Experience in transplantation, including clinical, translational, or operational work related to donor organ recovery, preservation, allocation, or implantation
  • Experience working in or with the HRSA, OPTN or UNOS, organ procurement organizations (OPOs), transplant centers, tissue banks, or organ recovery networks or programs involving cross-sector coordination
  • Experience with the practical and policy dimensions of the U.S. transplant ecosystem
  • Experience with organ perfusion technologies for assessment, preservation, repair, or treatment of donor organs
  • Experience with translational and commercialization challenges, including manufacturability, quality systems, reimbursement context, regulatory considerations, and clinical adoption barriers
  • Possession of strong team-oriented and interpersonal skills

Compensation

title: Sr. Data Platform Reliability Engineer
description:
Job Opportunity: Sr. Data Platform Reliability Engineer (Manila)

Location: Manila, Philippines
Employment Type: Full-Time
Work Arrangement: Onsite, with automatic work-from-home arrangements on weekends and holidays
Schedule: Shifting schedules (6:00 AM, 10:00 AM, or 2:00 PM)

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Reliability Engineer to operate, maintain, and continuously improve enterprise data platforms running on Kubernetes, whether on-premises or on AWS/GCP.

The role involves supporting production data workloads and ensuring platform reliability, performance, security, and operational efficiency. You will work with technologies and deployment frameworks similar to Data on EKS (DoEKS) and AI on EKS (AIoEKS).

This position is ideal for an experienced data platform professional with strong expertise in Kubernetes, data engineering, production operations, and incident management.

Key Responsibilities

  • Operate, maintain, and continuously improve data platforms running on Kubernetes across on-premises and cloud environments.
  • Deploy new releases and configuration changes through GitOps and DevOps practices.
  • Monitor platform and service health using logs, metrics, and observability tools.
  • Participate in incident response, root cause analysis, and 24/7 operational rotations.
  • Improve platform observability, operational tooling, automation, and self-service capabilities to reduce recurring issues.
  • Investigate and troubleshoot user concerns by identifying system-related issues, broken integrations, and user-specific errors or misconfigurations.
  • Recommend and execute appropriate resolutions to platform and service issues.
  • Provide technical mentorship and guidance to junior engineers.
  • Advocate for platform standards, security best practices, and operational excellence.

About this role

Fundamental Equities 

Fundamental Equities (FE) sits within BlackRock’s Portfolio Management Group (PMG). The business provides a global investment platform offering BlackRock clients a comprehensive range of actively managed, high conviction equity strategies.

FE’s global hybrid research model emphasizes the strength of an independent team approach with the benefits of platform-wide collaboration and connectivity. Company-level engagement and rigorous research underpin our investment teams’ deep domain expertise and lead to high conviction portfolios that aim to generate alpha for our clients.

Fundamental Equity Core Portfolio Manager, APAC

This is an Associate Core Portfolio Manager role within BlackRock’s Fundamental Equity business. Based in Taipei, the role will primarily provide regional Core PM support across FE APAC, including Taiwan, Japan, Australia and Hong Kong. The role combines daily, market-sensitive portfolio implementation and control responsibilities with broader regional projects. A secondary, but material, focus will be the development of technology-enabled solutions for the Core PM platform, requiring strong technical capability, proficiency in Python and the practical application of AI tools to improve investment workflows.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop a deep understanding of FE APAC investment processes, strategies, vehicles and markets, with a primary focus on supporting teams in Taiwan, Japan, Australia and Hong Kong.
  • Support the implementation of equity, derivative and FX orders across a range of active strategies, partnering with portfolio managers and global trading desks to target accurate and efficient execution.
  • Proactively monitor portfolios, cash, exposures and implementation outcomes to support investment intent and maintain effective governance and controls.
  • Provide flexible regional coverage for daily Core PM activities, market events, new mandates and cross-platform initiatives, working independently and collaboratively across APAC time zones.
  • Design, develop and maintain robust technology solutions for Core PM workflows using Python, Aladdin applications/APIs, data tools and appropriate software development practices.

Skills/Competencies 

  • Apply AI tools and agents in a controlled and practical manner to streamline workflows, improve insight generation, enhance scalability and reduce manual operational risk.
  • Collaborate with regional and global Core PM colleagues, Technology and Citizen Developer communities to prototype, test, document and scale reusable solutions.
  • Interact regularly with key stakeholders including portfolio managers, product strategists, global trading, client businesses, risk and operational support teams.
  • Communicate clearly and work effectively both independently and as part of a global team across multiple markets and time zones.
  • Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to prioritize concurrent market-sensitive responsibilities and longer-term development work.
  • A solutions-oriented mindset with a high level of ownership, curiosity, initiative and attention to detail.

Knowledge/Experience

  • Relevant experience in a finance, investment or technology role. A degree in business, finance, computing, engineering, data science or financial engineering would be a strong advantage.
  • Strong interest in equity markets and the investment process. Experience of portfolio implementation, trading workflows, investment operations or controls would be advantageous.
  • Proficiency in Python, including data analysis, workflow automation and API integration, together with sound coding, testing and documentation practices.
  • Hands-on experience with version control and collaborative development tools such as ADO or GitHub.
  • Knowledge of data structures, databases and SQL, with the ability to build reliable data pipelines and work with large or complex datasets.
  • Experience applying AI tools or agents to solve practical business problems, with an understanding of appropriate governance, validation and risk controls.
  • Familiarity with Aladdin applications/APIs and data visualization or reporting tools such as Power BI would be advantageous.

Our benefits

To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.

Our hybrid work model

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.


Guidance on AI use for candidates


At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


About BlackRock


At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.


This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Iraq is recognized as one of the most affected countries by the harmful effects of climate change. Iraq ratified the Paris Agreement on January 14, 2021. In October 2021, the Government of Iraq (GoI) signed their first National Determined Contribution (NDC), which has been presented at the COP26. The Government of Iraq has requested UNDP support in implementation of the NDC, including through capacity development, advisory for sectoral planning and formulation of related strategies, frameworks, and instruments.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels offers a spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in UNDP's Strategic Plan.

UNDP is an accredited Implementing Agency for the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Trust Fund and the family of funds such as the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), the Special Climate Change Fund (SCCF), and the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBBF). As an Implementing Agency, UNDP offers countries highly specialized services for eligibility assessment, project formulation and due diligence, co-financing mobilization, implementation oversight, results management and evaluation, and knowledge management.

Iraq faces significant environmental and public health risks associated with persistent organic pollutants (POPs), hazardous chemicals, obsolete pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), unintentional POPs (UPOPs), industrial POPs (IPOPs), and chemically contaminated sites. Previous assessments identified substantial quantities of obsolete pesticides and potentially PCB-contaminated electrical equipment and highlighted significant technical and institutional capacity gaps in chemicals and contaminated-sites management.

The Government of Iraq is a Party to major international chemicals and waste conventions, including the Stockholm, Basel, Rotterdam and Minamata Conventions. Iraq has previously developed a National Implementation Plan (NIP) under the Stockholm Convention; however, the existing NIP requires updating to reflect newly listed POPs, improved inventories, updated risk information, institutional developments and current national priorities.

The Integrated Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) and Chemical Hotspots Management Project, therefore adopts an integrated approach combining:

  • strengthening the national framework for POPs and hazardous chemicals management;
  • updating the national POPs inventories and National Implementation Plan;
  • strengthening laboratory, inspection, monitoring and institutional capacities;
  • environmentally sound management and disposal of obsolete pesticides;
  • management and disposal/phase-out of PCB-contaminated equipment, oils and waste; and
  • assessment and remediation planning for priority chemical pollution hotspots

The project comprises three components. Component 1 focuses on improved management of POPs and hazardous chemicals; Component 2 focuses on high-risk POPs in the agriculture and power sectors; and Component 3 addresses chemical pollution hotspots and contaminated sites.

Implementation will require extensive technical assistance, consultancy services, procurement of laboratory and field equipment, hazardous waste management services, capacity building, site assessments, remediation planning and policy/regulatory development.

Scope of Work

LEAD ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SAFEGUARDS COMPLIANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT

  • Lead and coordinate implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), the project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), applicable Environmental and Social Standards, UNDP Social and Environmental Standards, and relevant national environmental, occupational health and safety, labour and stakeholder-engagement requirements.
  • Establish and maintain a project-level environmental and social safeguards compliance and assurance system covering technical studies, field investigations, sampling, laboratory activities, procurement, transport, temporary storage, treatment, disposal, contaminated-site work and contractor operations.
  • Review project activities and procurement packages for environmental and social risks and advise the Project Manager and UNDP on the safeguards instruments, mitigation measures, monitoring requirements and contractual provisions required before implementation.
  • Review and provide technical clearance/advice on Environmental and Social Management Plans, site-specific management plans, occupational health and safety plans, waste-management plans, emergency preparedness and response arrangements, stakeholder-engagement measures, labour-management measures and other safeguards instruments required under the ESCP/ESF.
  • Ensure that safeguards requirements are adequately incorporated into Terms of Reference, technical specifications, bidding documents, contracts, contractor method statements and implementation plans.
  • Undertake or coordinate safeguards monitoring of consultants, contractors, laboratories, hazardous-waste operators and field activities; identify non-compliance and recommend corrective and preventive actions, including escalation of material risks to UNDP management.
  • Provide safeguards oversight for handling, packaging, temporary storage, transport, treatment and disposal of obsolete pesticides, PCB-contaminated equipment/oils and other hazardous wastes, including worker and community health and safety and emergency-response considerations.
  • Ensure appropriate environmental and social due diligence for chemical hotspot investigations and remediation planning, including community exposure pathways, vulnerable groups, land/access implications, occupational risks and stakeholder consultation.
  • Support incident and accident reporting, root-cause review, corrective-action tracking and safeguards reporting to UNDP, the Ministry of Environment and the World Bank, as applicable.
  • Maintain safeguards records and prepare periodic safeguards compliance notes/reports, including status of ESCP commitments, material risks, corrective actions and outstanding issues.
  • Provide technical guidance and capacity development to the PMU, government counterparts, consultants and contractors on ESF/ESCP, UNDP safeguards, hazardous-chemicals risk management and good international industry practice.

ESTABLISH AND LEAD THE PROJECT TECHNICAL QUALITY ASSURANCE SYSTEM.

  • Establish and maintain a systematic, risk-based technical quality assurance framework covering all project components, with defined review gates, technical acceptance criteria, peer-review requirements, corrective-action tracking and documentation of technical clearances.
  • Review and advise on the technical adequacy of major Terms of Reference, scopes of work, technical specifications, sampling and analytical protocols, technical designs, bidding documents and evaluation criteria before procurement or implementation.
  • Review consultants’ and contractors’ inception reports, methodologies, work plans, sampling plans, QA/QC plans, draft and final technical reports, feasibility studies, remediation designs, disposal/treatment proposals, laboratory methodologies, monitoring plans and technical training materials.
  • Validate the scientific and technical soundness, internal consistency, traceability and fitness-for-purpose of technical data, assumptions, findings, conclusions and recommendations against project requirements, international standards and relevant convention guidance.
  • Verify achievement of key technical milestones and advise the Project Manager on acceptance, conditional acceptance, revision or rejection of technical deliverables, without replacing the formal procurement/contract approval authorities.
  • Provide written technical review notes and recommendations for corrective action where technical gaps, methodological weaknesses, data-quality concerns, safeguards risks or implementation deficiencies are identified.
  • Support technical evaluation of specialized environmental procurement when requested, including assessment of technical methodologies, equipment specifications, laboratory capability, contractor qualifications and proposed treatment/disposal technologies.
  • Promote harmonized methodologies, sampling protocols, laboratory procedures, QA/QC systems and environmental assessment approaches so that Component 3 technical systems can support subsequent implementation of Components 1 and 2.

TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT AND QUALITY ASSURANCE OF POPS, HAZARDOUS CHEMICALS, PCBs AND OBSOLETE PESTICIDES

  • Provide senior technical review of national inventories and assessments of industrial POPs (iPOPs), unintentionally produced POPs (uPOPs), POPs pesticides, obsolete pesticides, newly listed POPs and other priority hazardous chemicals.
  • Assess whether inventory methodologies, data sources, sampling strategies, analytical methods, laboratory QA/QC and data-management systems are consistent with Stockholm Convention guidance and internationally accepted practice.
  • Review characterization, classification and prioritization of POPs stocks, waste streams, contaminated materials and exposure pathways, and ensure that inventory findings are appropriately reflected in risk-reduction measures, management plans and the updated National Implementation Plan (NIP).
  • Provide technical quality assurance for the updated NIP, including validation of inventory findings, prioritization, action plans, resource requirements, risk-reduction measures and consistency with Iraq’s obligations under the Stockholm Convention.
  • Review uPOPs assessments and application of the UNEP Toolkit, including source identification, emission estimation, prioritization and proposed Best Available Techniques/Best Environmental Practices (BAT/BEP).
  • Provide technical oversight and independent review of the PCB inventory, including sampling and testing strategies for transformers, capacitors, oils and associated contaminated materials; classification and risk categorization; and prioritization for phase-out, treatment and disposal.
  • Review and validate PCB management and phase-out plans and provide technical advice on decontamination, treatment, destruction and disposal options, including proposed mobile or fixed treatment technologies where applicable.
  • Review technical arrangements for PCB collection, draining, packaging, labelling, temporary storage, transport, treatment and final disposal, ensuring cradle-to-grave tracking and adequate documentation.
  • Provide technical review of obsolete pesticide stockpile assessments, site characterization, sampling and analytical results, risk assessments and proposed management/disposal strategies.
  • Assess the technical and environmental suitability of packaging, containment, temporary storage, transportation, treatment and disposal options, including in-country and transboundary disposal arrangements.
  • Review qualifications, methodologies and performance of specialized hazardous-waste contractors from a technical and safeguards perspective and verify disposal/destruction documentation and certificates.
  • Ensure technical consistency with Stockholm Convention and Basel Convention requirements, applicable national requirements, the World Bank ESF and recognized international hazardous-waste management practices.

TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT AND QUALITY ASSURANCE OF CHEMICAL HOTSPOTS AND CONTAMINATED SITES

  • Provide senior technical oversight and independent review of national hotspot identification and prioritization and detailed assessment of priority chemical contamination sites.
  • Review conceptual site models, investigation designs, sampling plans, laboratory analytical programmes, data-quality objectives, hydrogeological assessments and contaminant fate-and-transport analyses.
  • Review human health and ecological risk assessments, including exposure pathways, receptors, uncertainty analysis and risk-based prioritization.
  • Assess remediation feasibility studies and site-specific remediation plans for technical feasibility, environmental and social soundness, proportionality to risk, implementability and long-term monitoring requirements.
  • Advise on remediation objectives, cleanup criteria/standards, verification requirements, institutional controls and post-remediation monitoring.
  • Provide technical guidance for the National Programme on Contaminated Sites Management, including site screening, risk classification, investigation, remediation decision-making, technical standards, GIS/database requirements and long-term monitoring.
  • Ensure that contaminated-site assessments and remediation plans adequately address POPs and other hazardous chemical contamination and are consistent with the national information-management system being developed under Component 3.

LABORATORY, SAMPLING AND DATA QUALITY ASSURANCE

  • Review laboratory modernization plans, analytical equipment specifications, installation/commissioning arrangements, calibration requirements, certified reference materials, QA/QC procedures and operation and maintenance provisions.
  • Review and promote fit-for-purpose sampling, chain-of-custody, sample preservation, laboratory analytical and data-validation procedures for POPs, PCBs and chemical hotspot investigations.
  • Assess laboratory and field-monitoring performance, including detection limits, calibration, proficiency, blanks/duplicates, data validation and documentation, and recommend corrective measures where data quality is insufficient.
  • Ensure traceability of technical evidence from field sampling and laboratory analysis through risk assessment, inventory development, remediation/disposal decisions and reporting.

TECHNICAL MONITORING, VERIFICATION AND ADAPTIVE MANAGEMENT AND CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT, KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER AND STRATEGIC TECHNICAL ADVICE

  • Conduct periodic technical and safeguards implementation reviews across the project portfolio and provide concise assurance reports to UNDP management and the Project Manager on technical quality, compliance, emerging risks and required corrective actions.
  • Support verification of contractor and consultant performance against approved methodologies, technical specifications, safeguards obligations, deliverables and key milestones.
  • Contribute to technical review of project progress reports, Steering Committee documentation, World Bank missions and implementation-support reviews, focusing on technical quality and environmental/social compliance.
  • Maintain technical issues and corrective-actions register and follow up on closure of significant findings.
  • Apply adaptive management by identifying emerging technical, safeguards and implementation risks and recommending proportionate adjustments that preserve the approved project scope and contractual requirements.
  • Provide targeted technical mentoring and on-the-job support to the PMU, Ministry of Environment and relevant national institutions on safeguards, POPs/PCB management, contaminated-site assessment, remediation planning, hazardous-waste management, laboratory QA/QC and technical review.
  • Review technical manuals, standard operating procedures, guidance notes and training materials to ensure scientific accuracy, safeguards integration and consistency across project components.
  • Support technical consultations, validation workshops and coordination with the Ministry of Environment, relevant ministries, laboratories, academia, technical institutions, the World Bank, GEF and specialized service providers.
  • Document lessons learned and technical recommendations that strengthen sustainable national systems for POPs, hazardous chemicals and contaminated-site management beyond the project period.
  • Provide substantive advice and technical support to the development and implementation of a capacity development/ learning plan on thematic area of the project for Country Office and participate in global/regional learning initiatives.
  • Keep abreast of the developments in the thematic area of the project and provide guidance on how to incorporate them into UNDP’s current and future programming in the relevant sector. Provide technical guidance and quality assurance to content development for knowledge products.

BUILD STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS AND SUPPORT RESOURCE MOBILIZATION AND ACHIEVEMENT OF STRATEGIC RESULTS.

  • Maintain strategic relationships with UNDP partners, Government institutions, donors, development partners, civil society, academia, private-sector stakeholders and specialized technical organizations.
  • Build and maintain partnerships with donor agencies and development partners working on climate change, environment, chemicals and waste management.
  • Identify and follow up on strategic opportunities for resource mobilization from traditional and non-traditional donors.
  • Support the conceptualization of technically robust interventions that respond to national priorities and emerging environmental challenges.
  • Work closely with the Partnerships and Planning Unit and relevant UNDP teams on resource mobilization, donor engagement, reporting and corporate compliance.
  • Engage with GEF and other relevant funding mechanisms and technical networks.
  • Strengthen collaboration with relevant UN agencies contributing to UNSDCF priority working groups to promote complementarity and avoid duplication.
  • Maintain effective relationships with the GEF Secretariat and relevant technical networks.
  • Strengthen cooperation with the mechanisms and technical networks associated with the Stockholm, Basel, Rotterdam and other relevant environmental conventions.
  • Promote engagement with laboratories, universities, research institutions, private-sector stakeholders, waste management companies and specialized disposal contractors.
  • Identify opportunities for technical cooperation, knowledge exchange and joint programming.
  • Identify emerging national priorities and technical gaps that could provide opportunities for new programming and resource mobilization.
  • Lead or contribute to the technical conceptualization of new project ideas, programmes and funding proposals.
  • Provide substantive technical inputs to concept notes, project documents, funding proposals and donor submissions.
  • Identify opportunities for scaling up successful approaches and replicating technical solutions.
  • Engage with traditional and non-traditional donors and development partners to communicate the strategic relevance and technical value of proposed interventions.
  • Ensure that proposed interventions are evidence-based, technically feasible and aligned with national priorities and UNDP strategic frameworks.
  • Contribute to monitoring and reporting on relevant CPD and portfolio results.
  • Monitor implementation of targets and indicators linked to the portfolio and identify corrective actions where required.
  • Support preparation and review of annual reports, donor reports and other substantive reporting requirements.
  • Provide technical inputs for donor briefings, missions, steering committee meetings and strategic portfolio reviews.
  • Maintain a pipeline of technically sound opportunities for future resource mobilization.
  • Strengthen the positioning of UNDP as a strategic technical partner in climate change, environment, chemicals and waste management.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall and direct supervision of the DRR, and with matrix reporting to the EECC Programme Specialist, the Chief Technical Specialist (CTS) will serve as the Project’s senior technical assurance function. The position will have two principal areas of responsibility: (i) Environmental and Social Safeguards; and (ii) Technical Quality Assurance and independent technical assessment of POPs, PCBs, obsolete pesticides, hazardous chemicals and chemical pollution hotspots. The CTS will provide technical advice and assurance across Components 1, 2 and 3, while the Project Manager retains responsibility for day-to-day project management, delivery, coordination, budget, procurement administration and reporting.

The Chief Technical Specialist (CTS) will work closely with the national head of Environment, Energy and Climate Change (EECC), pillar UNDP Iraq. The CTS will work closely with Government counterparts, national authorities, project experts, donors, development partners, UNDP programmes and projects, and other relevant national and international stakeholders.

The CTS will be part of a multidisciplinary team of national and international experts supporting policy advocacy, technical oversight, capacity building, innovation and knowledge sharing in the areas of climate change, environmental management, POPs, hazardous chemicals and chemical pollution hotspots management.

Competencies

Core Competencies

  • Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact
  • Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems
  • Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences
  • Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands
  • Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results
  • Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration
  • Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Technical and Cross-functional Competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

  • System Thinking
    • Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system
  • Effective Decision Making
    • Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one’s authority, area of expertise and resources.
  • Negotiation and influence
    • Reach an understanding, persuade others, resolve points of difference, gain advantage in the outcome of dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions through compromise, and create win-win situations.

2030 Agenda: Planet

  • Nature
    • Environmental Governance: Global Environmental Governance

Business Management

  • Project management
    • Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals.
  • Risk management
    • Identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks

Partnership Management

  • Strategic Engagement
    • Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives

Required Skills and Experience

Minimum Education requirements

  • Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Climate Change, Toxicology, Hazardous Waste Management, Environmental Management, or a closely related discipline is required, or
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Minimum years of relevant work experience

  • Minimum 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible relevant experience at the national or international level in providing technical advice, conducting research, formulating policies, and/or developing and managing complex projects in sectors applicable to thematic area(s).

Required skills

  • Experience definyning priorities, designing projects, managing budgets, preparing plans and monitoring to achieve quality results.
  • Demonstrated experience with one or more of; POPs inventories, Stockholm Convention NIPs, PCB management and phase-out, obsolete pesticide management, UPOPs/BAT/BEP, hazardous waste treatment/disposal, contaminated-site assessment and remediation, environmental risk assessment, chemicals policy and regulatory development.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

  • Experience with project planning and consulting, including the effective provision of substantive leadership and guidance, oversight, monitoring, and reporting for projects/programmes with similar scale, scope, and complexity.
  • Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.
  • Demonstrated experience in advocating for development or climate agenda in international, multi-cultural settings with problem solving capacities;
  • Experience with UN operational and management common tools such as Results Based Management;
  • Demonstrated experience in coordinating with multidisciplinary stakeholders; i.e. governments, academia, civil society, media and donors
  • Prior experiences of working in Iraq or the Arab region, with in depth knowledge of Iraq’s social/cultural and political context;

Required Language(s)

  • Fluency in English is required.
  • Knowledge of Arabic is an asset.
