title: Souschef, Brugsen Raklev
description:
Grib chancen hos Danmarks største detailhandelsvirksomhed og få en spændende mulighed for at:

  • være med til at lede en butik med stærk lokal forankring og et godt sammenhold
  • få en tæt relation til dine kunder og være blandt kunderne i dagligdagen
  • udvikle dig som leder og samtidig få mange karrieremuligheder i Coop

Brugsen Raklev

Vi er en del af Kalundborg Brugsforening, og er Raklevs lokale dagligvarebutik. Butikken er for nyligt moderniseret, og har bl.a. fået nye køle- og frysemøbler.

Raklev er en lille by beliggende en kort køretur nord for Kalundborg.

Bliv en del af den lokale købmand

Som Souschef i Brugsen er du uddelerens sparingspartner, og du er med i alle de driftsmæssige beslutninger i butikken. Du får dermed erfaring med alle ledelsesmæssige opgaver, hvilket betyder at du:

  • har medansvar for den praktiske ledelse i butikken
  • tager medejerskab og forpligter dig professionelt og engageret i forhold til at nå de givne budget- og omsætningsmål
  • udvikler butikken og præger sortimentet

Størstedelen af din tid bruger du blandt medarbejdere og kunder i butikken. Det er vigtigt, at du lærer vores kunder at kende, så vi kan tilbyde et sortiment, der imødekommer deres behov. Her er der i vid udstrækning frie rammer til at udøve ægte købmandsskab og være med til at påvirke sortimentet samt bringe lokale varer ind.

Vær med til at udvikle lokalsamfundet

Som byens lokale købmand er du en aktiv spiller i lokalsamfundet. Sammen med uddeleren er du med til at skabe aktiviteter i byen og lader butikken danne ramme for f.eks. fastelavnsfest, sociale arrangementer, efterårsfester mm.

Købmand til fingerspidserne

  • Du er uddannet som f.eks salgsassistent
  • Du har mindst 3 års praktisk butikserfaring fra detailhandlen
  • Du har god forståelse for tal og regnskaber

Som person er du først og fremmest udadvendt og du kan lide at tale med mennesker. Du er initiativrig og tænker ud ad boksen.

Som leder har du gennemslagskraft og kan sikre resultater, således at vi sikrer kunderne en inspirerende butik.

Slutteligt går du forrest og viser engagement, som afspejler sig i medarbejdernes motivation.

Vil du vide mere om stillingen?

Du er velkommen til at kontakte Uddeler Kasper Bo Larsen på telefon 59508021 – eller kig forbi butikken til en snak.

Send din ansøgning via "Ansøg nu" senest den 02/10-2026

Vi behandler ansøgninger løbende.

I Brugsen er vi tættere på kunderne

I Brugsen arbejder vi ud fra vores DNA, som er kvalitet, ansvarlighed og fællesskab. Det betyder at vi tager ansvar for vores beslutninger, arbejder sammen på tværs for at skabe de bedste resultater, og vi tror på at kvalitet opstår, når vi deler viden, løfter i flok og tager et fælles ansvar.

Brugsen er den lokale købmand og et vigtigt aktiv I de byer, vi er repræsenteret. Vi nyder fordelene af at være en del af en kæde samtidig med, at vi kan drive butikkerne med fokus på lokale Initiativer, lokale varer, osv. Vi er en vigtig brik i byens liv – vi både støtter og tager initiativ til lokale arrangementer, som giver et twist i det daglige arbejde. Vi er desuden mindre butikker med et rigtig godt sammenhold, hvor hver medarbejder får meget ansvar, og vi hjælper hinanden med alle opgaver.

Bliver du ansat i Brugsen bliver du en del af Coop-familien. Vi er omkring 40.000 medarbejdere og sammen med brugsforeningerne har vi en samlet omsætning på mere end 40 milliarder kr. i vores ca. 900 butikker over hele Danmark. Derfor er der mange muligheder for både nye opgaver og uddannelse og ikke mindst jobskifte internt i Coop. Vi er ejet af vores 2 million medlemmer og det andelsejede Energiselskab OK.

Vi værdsætter mangfoldighed og søger kvalificerede kandidater uanset baggrund. Sammen skaber vi plads til forskellighed, faglighed og kvalitet. Derfor sikrer vi en retfærdig rekrutteringsproces, hvor det er op til dig, om du vil vedhæfte ansøgning og billede.

title: Kirketjener til Folkekirken Vesterbro
description:
- med base i Mariakirken
Fuldtidsstilling

Trives du med skiftende arbejdstider – også aften og weekend – og med meget varierede opgaver? Og sætter du en ære i at skabe orden, gode rammer og en varm velkomst for alle, der træder ind ad døren?
Så er du måske vores nye kirketjener i Folkekirken Vesterbro, med base i Mariakirken!

Om stedet
Mariakirken ligger i Istedgade nær Hovedbanegården og er en kirke med et stærkt socialt engagement. Her møder du mennesker med meget forskellige livsvilkår og er med til at skabe trygge, ordentlige og velkomne rammer omkring både gudstjenester, sociale indsatser og daglige aktiviteter. Kirken danner blandt andet ramme om Mariatjenesten, som drives i et samarbejde mellem Kirkens Korshær og Vesterbro Sogn, samt sognets Natherberg for hjemløse.

Din base bliver i Mariakirken, men du vil også få faste og midlertidige opgaver i sognets øvrige kirker.

Dine opgaver vil blandt andet være:

  • rengøring, oprydning og løbende praktisk drift
  • klargøring og medvirken til gudstjenester, kirkelige handlinger og arrangementer
  • indkøb, varemodtagelse og forsyning af varer
  • kontakt til brugere, frivillige, kollegaer og samarbejdspartnere
Vi søger en kollega der:

  • trives i et hus med mange slags mennesker, hvor hverdagen sjældent er ens
  • møder mennesker respektfuldt, roligt og ligeværdigt — også når situationer er uforudsigelige
  • har situationsfornemmelse og ved, hvornår en samtale eller situation bør henvises til en præst eller socialpædagogisk medarbejder
  • sætter en ære i praktisk arbejde – herunder rengøring, klargøring og oprydning
  • er imødekommende og kan være kirkens ansigt udadtil over for gæster, frivillige og samarbejdspartnere
  • arbejder selvstændigt og har blik for, hvad der skal gøres – også før andre ser det
  • kan koordinere opgaver med kollegaer og frivillige
  • møder andre med respekt – også når der er travlt
  • trives med at ca. halvdelen af arbejdstiden består af rengøring.
Vi lægger vægt på dine personlige og sociale kompetencer. Din uddannelsesmæssige baggrund er mindre vigtig. Hvis du allerede har kirketjeneruddannelsen, er det dog et plus, men ellers sørger vi for at du får den.


Vi kan byde på:

  • gode kollegaer og en hverdag præget af samarbejde, engagement og fælles ansvar
  • en arbejdsplads, hvor dit praktiske arbejde er med til at skabe velfungerende rammer for husets aktiviteter
  • en nærværende daglig ledelse, som er ansat til opgaven og kan kontaktes alle ugens dage
  • fokus på balance mellem arbejde og privatliv, blandt andet med mulighed for at tilpasse arbejdstiden ved særlige behov
  • en stor og mangfoldig kirkelig arbejdsplads med en varieret hverdag, mange samarbejdsflader og opgaver tæt på mennesker
Har du lyst til at være en del af et engageret fællesskab, hvor praktisk sans, gæstfrihed og samarbejde gør en forskel hver dag? Så glæder vi os til at høre fra dig.

Arbejdstider
Der varierer fra uge til uge afhængigt af de aktiviteter, du deltager i. Du får som udgangspunkt din arbejdsplan ca. 30 dage i forvejen. Du forventes i høj grad selv at kunne strukturere dine opgaver og arbejdstid omkring de aktiviteter, du medvirker i.

Som udgangspunkt har du:

  • Fast fri hver onsdag
  • Én ekstra fridag om ugen, som er fleksibel. Den behøver ikke ligge i den samme uge, men kan flyttes og bruges senere.
  • Mulighed for ca. hver fjerde uge at samle to af de fleksible fridage, så du får fri både lørdag og søndag.
Eksempel på fire uger:

  • Uge 1: Fri onsdag og torsdag
  • Uge 2: Fri onsdag
  • Uge 3: Fri onsdag og torsdag
  • Uge 4: Fri onsdag, lørdag og søndag
Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår
Arbejdstiden udgør gennemsnitligt 37 timer pr. uge.

Ansættelse sker i henhold til Fællesoverenskomsten mellem Finansministeriet og CO10 samt Organisationsaftale mellem Kirkeministeriet og CO10. Årslønnen aftales inden for intervallet 255.000 kr. – 321.112 kr. i grundbeløb pr. 31.marts 2012. Dertil kommer OK18-tillæg på 1.100 kr. samt rådighedstillæg på 26.100 kr. i grundbeløb pr. 31.marts 2012. I nutidskroner svarer det til en samlet årsløn i intervallet 357.006,99 kr. – 440.644,29 kr. pr. 1. august 2026 for en fuldtidsstilling. Aftalerne kan ses på www.folkekirkenspersonale.dk.

Nuværende tjenestemandsansatte kirketjenere kan bevare deres tjenestemandsstatus ved ansættelse med direkte overgang. Der skal i så fald ske en klassificering af stillingen.

Der vil blive indhentet børneattest i forbindelse med ansættelsen.

Ansøgning
Du kan sende din ansøgning via linket i dette opslag senest 16/10 2026 – bilag skal vedlægges som pdf-filer.

Vi forventer at afholde samtaler i uge 44.

Stillingen er ledig til besættelse snarest muligt.

Folkekirken Vesterbro er Danmarks største sogn. Menighedsrådet har høje ambitioner og stærkt fokus på at være relevant kirke for folk på Vesterbro. For at møde forskellighederne på Vesterbro arbejder kirkerne med at udvikle forskellige profiler inden for en fælles ramme. Kirkerne drives og bæres af frivillige kræfter i tæt samspil med 14 præster og ca. 50 medarbejdere.

title: National Advertising Campaign Specialist
description:
Our Lamar Corporate office in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, is now hiring a National Advertising Campaign Specialist to oversee all post-buy aspects of a National Campaign and manage the execution of dynamic digital campaigns. This position also acts as a liaison between the National Sales team, national customers, IT, and local Lamar offices to troubleshoot and drive resolutions during the life cycle of the campaign.

The National Campaign Specialist is responsible for overseeing all post-buy aspects of a National Campaign, including day-to-day communication of material delivery, installation updates, digital scheduling, and proof of performance delivery. The National Campaign Specialist also manages the execution of dynamic digital campaigns. The position ensures scheduling and campaign compliance and upholds digital scheduling best practices.

Why Lamar?

This assessment compares your professional soft skills to the skills required for success in this role. Please answer honestly; this is not a test! Not completing this assessment could result in disqualification from consideration for this position.

      Candidates with a disability in need of an accommodation to fulfill our application requirements should email recruiting@lamar.com.

      A day in the life:

      • Ensure posting instructions for national campaigns are provided in a timely manner by customers and are ready for distribution
      • Audit posting instructions and creative file images from the customer for accuracy; resolve creative file issues accordingly, directly with the customer or the customer’s design agency
      • Distribute posting instructions and creative images to local sales offices for national campaigns
      • Track production materials, maintain tracking logs, and digital schedule organization best practices for each campaign
      • Execute a high volume of digital scheduling on a daily basis
      • Compile and distribute status update reports for customers on a daily basis
      • Troubleshoot and help solve production-related issues with external and internal customers and partners to ensure an on-time posting of national campaigns
      • Identifies digital technical issues resulting in a delivery compromise, like board outages, and determines technical, local market, and client implications; takes action accordingly
      • Anticipate problems, and communicate with customers, National Account Executives, Account Managers, and local Lamar offices

title: Senior Network Engineer
description:
Job Description

Job Description

Network Engineer (NE)

Leidos – Cyber & Analytics Business Area, Key Management & Analytics Division,

Your Experience. A Critical Mission. Real Impact.


Leidos has an exciting opportunity for an experienced Network Engineer to join our Cyber & Analytics Business Area, Key Management & Analytics Division, supporting critical national-security missions.


This is an opportunity to apply deep network engineering expertise to complex, mission-critical environments—from designing and optimizing secure networks to deploying communications capabilities, troubleshooting complex problems, integrating emerging technologies, and guiding other network engineers.


You'll work alongside systems engineers, cybersecurity professionals, technical teams, and mission partners to ensure network and telecommunications capabilities are secure, resilient, optimized, and ready to perform when the mission demands it.


This is a full-time, on-site position in a secure mission environment. Due to the nature of the work and security requirements, remote work is not available for this position.


If you're an experienced network engineer who enjoys solving difficult technical problems and wants to see your expertise translate directly into mission capability, we'd like to talk.


What You'll Do

As a Senior Network Engineer, you'll provide senior-level engineering expertise across the network and telecommunications lifecycle—from architecture and design through integration, deployment, operations, optimization, and sustainment.

  • Design, Engineer & Deploy Mission Networks - Design, build, integrate, test, document, and deploy secure network and telecommunications solutions supporting complex mission requirements. Engineer solutions incorporating routing protocols, BGP, policy-based routing, traffic shaping, tunneling, IPsec, NAT, firewall contexts, load balancing, WAN acceleration, and network monitoring, while integrating new technologies as mission needs evolve.
  • Operate, Secure & Optimize Network Infrastructure - Configure, install, maintain, and optimize network and telecommunications infrastructure, including routers, firewalls, intrusion detection systems, cryptographic devices, VoIP, VTC, POTS, and VSAT satellite communications systems. Monitor accredited environments, analyze traffic and TCP performance, minimize latency, maximize throughput, and help ensure the required security and operational posture is maintained.
  • Troubleshoot Complex Network & Telecommunications Challenges - Lead investigation, diagnostics, and resolution of complex network incidents and performance issues. Analyze system logs, traffic characteristics, connectivity, transmission speeds, packet behavior, and throughput; identify root causes and develop, test, document, and implement solutions and workarounds. Assess and apply patches, updates, configuration changes, backup procedures, and corrective actions using approved methods and procedures.
  • Provide Technical Leadership & Mission Integration - Partner with systems engineers, cybersecurity professionals, external Network Operations Centers (NOCs), telecommunications providers, and cross-organizational teams to translate mission requirements into effective technical solutions. Maintain network diagrams and configuration documentation, support Certification and Accreditation (C&A) requirements, and provide technical leadership and guidance to Level 0–2 Network Engineers, validating their work and ensuring approved engineering methods and procedures are followed.


What You'll Bring

This position requires an experienced cybersecurity professional with demonstrated Information Systems Security Officer experience supporting programs and contracts of comparable scope, type, and complexity.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Fifteen (15) years of experience as a Network Engineer on programs and contracts of similar scope, type, and complexity.
  • Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline from an accredited college or university. Five (5) years of experience in Network Engineering disciplines may be substituted for the bachelor's degree.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance with Polygraph and ability to work full-time on site in a secure mission environment.
  • Current Cisco Certified Network Professional (CCNP) certification in an applicable networking discipline, or an equivalent certification approved by the program.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, configuring, implementing, troubleshooting, and optimizing complex network and telecommunications environments, including routing protocols, BGP, policy-based routing, tunneling, IPsec, NAT, WAN technologies, traffic management, and network performance analysis.
  • Experience configuring, testing, installing, troubleshooting, and maintaining enterprise network and security infrastructure, including routers, firewalls, intrusion detection systems, cryptographic devices, and related network technologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve complex network and telecommunications problems, develop and document technical solutions, and provide technical guidance and leadership to junior and mid-level Network Engineers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience configuring, administering, troubleshooting, and optimizing Palo Alto Networks firewalls, including security policies, NAT, routing, logging, and traffic analysis.
  • Experience with VoIP, Video Teleconferencing (VTC), POTS, and/or VSAT TDMA IP-based satellite communications systems.
  • Experience performing advanced TCP/IP and network performance analysis, including troubleshooting latency, throughput, packet flow, and end-to-end network performance.
  • Experience supporting accredited network environments, including configuration management, security compliance, and Certification and Accreditation (C&A) activities.
  • Experience introducing, evaluating, and integrating new network and telecommunications technologies into complex operational environments.

Why Leidos?

At Leidos, you'll work alongside talented technical and mission professionals solving complex challenges where cybersecurity is fundamental to mission success.


You'll have opportunities to continue developing your expertise while contributing to consequential national-security work and connecting with the breadth of technical capabilities and career opportunities across Leidos.


Eligible employees have access to a competitive benefits package that includes:

  • Paid Time Off
  • 11 paid holidays
  • 401(k) with a 6% company match and immediate vesting
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Technical upskilling and professional-development opportunities
  • Education and training support
  • Paid parental leave
  • Additional health, wellness, and employee benefits

Ready to Make an Impact?

At Leidos, the opportunities are boundless. We challenge our staff with interesting assignments that allow them to thrive professionally and personally. For us, helping you grow your career is good business. We look forward to learning more about you – apply today

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. title: Lead Software Engineer
description:
ABOUT SLATE

At Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization. The spirit of DIY and customization runs throughout every element of a Slate, because people should have control over how their trucks look, feel, and represent them.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Slate runs lean by design. Every dollar we spend has to earn its place on the truck, and the same philosophy applies to our enterprise systems. We are looking for a Sr. full stack engineer who understands that good software architecture is a manufacturing advantage, not an IT overhead.

This is a developer role. You will build the digital backbone that connects functional teams across the enterprise: operations, supply chain, commercial, and digital. You've spent your career at the intersection of cloud infrastructure, full-stack development, and enterprise integration, and you know how to build platforms that scale without bureaucracy.

You will report to the Head of Enterprise Systems Engineering and partner closely with Product, Operations, and Supply Chain leadership to ensure our systems evolve with the business.


WHAT YOU GET TO DO

  • Lead Enterprise Solution Strategy: Define and drive the technical vision for enterprise applications, integration platforms, and digital capabilities that support operations and supply chain transformation. Align technology investments with business objectives while ensuring solutions scale across multiple functions and geographies.
  • Architect Scalable and Resilient Platforms: Establish architectural standards, reference patterns, and engineering best practices for enterprise systems. Lead the design of resilient, scalable, and secure platforms that support increasing operational complexity, business growth, and evolving supply chain demands.
  • Drive Enterprise Integration Excellence: Partner with Supply Chain, Finance, Operations, and business stakeholders to define integration strategies across critical business processes. Champion API-first, event-driven, and data-centric architectures that enable seamless connectivity, interoperability, and real-time business insights across the enterprise.
  • Influence Strategic Technology Decisions: Serve as a trusted technical advisor to engineering leadership, architects, and business partners by evaluating emerging technologies, SaaS platforms, and integration capabilities. Guide technology selection and investment decisions to ensure alignment with enterprise architecture, security, and operational objectives.
  • Raise Engineering Quality and Operational Excellence: Establish and promote standards for software quality, reliability, security, observability, and maintainability. Drive engineering excellence through scalable development practices, automation, governance frameworks, and continuous improvement initiatives that reduce operational risk and accelerate delivery.
  • Mentor and Amplify Organizational Impact: Provide technical leadership across teams by mentoring engineers, fostering architectural alignment, and enabling knowledge sharing. Influence engineering culture, improve developer productivity, and lead initiatives that strengthen the organization's technical capabilities and execution effectiveness.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TEAM

  • 12+ years in software engineering, preferably in automotive, e-commerce, or manufacturing-adjacent environments.
  • Proven Full-Stack Engineering Caliber: Hands-on background in React.js, microservices/serverless, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and AWS. Unblock the team while simultaneously driving architectural direction and engineering strategy.
  • Enterprise Systems Depth: Meaningful experience delivering supply chain, procurement, or e-commerce systems at OEM or Tier-1 scale -- understanding how data flows from supplier portal to factory floor to customer.
  • Cloud-Native Fluency: Deep familiarity with AWS services, infrastructure-as-code, and cloud-native design patterns; experience operating systems at production scale with real SLAs.
  • Integration Architecture: Strong grasp of API design, event-driven messaging, EDI integration patterns, and how to stitch together heterogeneous enterprise systems without creating a ball of mud.
  • CRM and ERP Integration: Familiarity with CRM and ERP platforms and the integration patterns that connect them to custom-built operational applications -- understanding where commercial systems end and custom engineering begins.
  • Startup Orientation: Demonstrated ability to operate in fast-moving, resource-constrained environments -- you know how to ship, how to cut scope without cutting corners, and how to rebuild while the plane is flying.
  • Communication and Influence: Ability to translate technical complexity into business outcomes for non-technical stakeholders; comfortable presenting to executive leadership and board-level audiences.

SALARY RANGE


The compensation for this position is the range Slate reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including job-related knowledge; skillset; experience, education and training; certifications; work location; and other relevant business and organizational factors.

$141,807.00 - $212,710.00 USD Annual


Additional Compensation and Benefits: Slate offers a wide range of competitive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability insurance, vacation, and 401k. The successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in the equity program and/or a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing such programs.


WHY JOIN TEAM SLATE?

At Slate, we’re fueled by grit, determination, and attention to detail. The start-up spirit of ingenuity and resourcefulness move our business forward. Team Slate fosters a culture of excellence, innovation, and mutual respect, and is motivated by shared principles.

title: Health Specialist
description: At the World Bank , a member of the World Bank Group (WBG) , you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd The MENAAP Region: The Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan Region (MENAAP) serves twenty two countries, of which twelve are active/potentially active IBRD/IDA borrowers (Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Syria, West Bank and Gaza, Tunisia, Yemen, Afghanistan, and Pakistan) and eight are users of the Region's non-lending services, mostly on a reimbursable basis (Bahrain, Kuwait, Libya, Malta, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates). The mission of MENAAP is to foster sustainable growth with a focus on job creation and poverty reduction, economic and social inclusion, and good governance. MENAAP attaches importance to creating a supportive work environment based on the values of teamwork, transparency, trust, and client service, underlined by professional excellence. MENAAP places high value on diversity. MENAAP is organized in seven Country Departments (CMUs), the Office of the Regional Chief Economist, and the Development Effectiveness Unit (MAPDE). Unit Context: The MENAAP People Vertical (HMADR) team is led by a Regional Practice Director (RPD) and encompasses three units (Health, Nutrition and Population (HNP); Social Policy (SP), and Education and Skills (EduSkills). The MENAAP People strategy aims to enhance Human Capital in the Region to help MENAAP become a region that realizes its vast potential by harnessing its greatest untapped assets: the human capital of its population, including youth, women, and the elderly. The Health, Nutrition and Population Global Practice (HNP) The World Bank Group supports countries’ efforts towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and to provide quality, affordable health services to everyone —regardless of their ability to pay — by strengthening primary health care systems and reducing the financial risks associated with ill health and increasing equity. The HNP Global Practice (GP) is led by a Global Director, who has overall responsibility for the GP. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/health The HNP program in the MENAAP is very varied and includes: (i) a portfolio under implementation with a strong focus on health systems strengthening, including health financing, to achieve UHC; (ii) a growing portfolio of health emergency operations; (iii) investment operations in very fragile settings; (iv) analytical work and capacity building program on health emergency prevention, preparedness and response, health financing, NCDs, pharmaceuticals, among others; (v) close regional and country partnership activities with WHO, UNICEF, the Global Fund, Gavi, the French Development Agency, the UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office, JICA, among others, and plans to develop further partnerships with the Islamic Development Bank and the Asia Infrastructure Investment Bank; (vi) a large and growing Reimbursable Advisory Services program in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries covering several areas of health policy, from public health, to non-communicable diseases (NCDs), to climate change and health. The MENAAP HNP Global Practice (HMAPH) is managed by a Practice Manager. The Social Policy Global Practice (SP) The SP GP delivers operational approaches and evidence-based solutions to help individuals and families manage risk, cope with chronic/transitional poverty, and access better livelihoods and jobs. These include strategy, analysis, financing and design of programs delivering social safety nets/social assistance (cash transfers, public works programs, social care services), social insurance (old-age pensions, unemployment insurance, disability and survivor benefits), and labor market and youth employment programs and policies (public employment services, active labor market programs, labor market regulations and institutions). The SP GP unit in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (MENAAP) (HMAPS) manages a growing operations portfolio of about 20 projects worth US$7 billion in net commitments and exciting knowledge program across the region. HMAPS is part of the MENAAP People department (HMADR), which also includes Health, Nutrition and Population (HMAPH) and Education (HMAPE). The Education and Skills (EduSkills) The Education and Skills Global Practice portfolio in the MENAAP region spans a wide set of country contexts, from the Gulf Cooperation Council states to fragility-affected settings like Afghanistan, Yemen, and West Bank and Gaza, and is organized across seven Country Management Units. The portfolio addresses several interrelated priorities: reducing learning poverty, expanding access and equity particularly for girls and displaced populations, strengthening education systems through governance reforms, curriculum development, teacher training, and student assessment, and building workforce-relevant skills through TVET and higher education programs aligned with labor market demand. The GCC countries are engaged primarily through Reimbursable Advisory Services. Across the region, the practice is increasingly focused on digital skills and green transformation as structural drivers of future employment, and sector tailored skills training investments. Delivery in FCV-affected countries is supported through third-party monitoring and UN agency partnerships. Country context: Afghanistan Afghanistan is one of the poorest countries in the world, facing a severe and compounding human development crisis. Living standards are threatened by the ongoing drought, widespread food insecurity and recurrent disease outbreaks — including poliovirus, one of only two countries globally where wild poliovirus remains endemic. The displacement crisis continues, with millions internally displaced and over 5.2 million returnees since 2023 placing additional strain on already fragile services. Despite conflict-related challenges, notable improvements in the coverage and quality of health services and health outcomes have been made over the past twenty years. The newborn mortality rate fell from 53 to 23 per 1,000 live births from 2003 to 2018, and the under-five mortality rate from 257 to 50 per 1,000 live births over the same period. Life expectancy has increased over the same period, from 56 to almost 64 years. Social protection systems are largely absent, leaving the most vulnerable, including women, girls, and displaced populations, without predictable support. At the same time, education, skills and employment crisis has deepened. Learning poverty is among highest in the world pointing to very low access to and quality of education: indeed, almost half of boys and over half of girls remain out of school at the primary level; system-wide bans by the Interim Taliban Administration (ITA)’s on girls’ access to secondary and tertiary education persist. Nearly half of youth are not in education, employment, or training, and female youth unemployment reaches 54%. Across health, social protection, education, skills and livelihoods, Afghanistan's human development indicators remain among the lowest in the region, demanding urgent, integrated responses. The health sector in Afghanistan is at an inflection point following the collapse of the Republic on August 15th, 2021, and the takeover by the Taliban, which subsequently established an interim administration. As this administration is not recognized internationally, support is provided off-budget through UN agencies and INGOs. The economic crisis triggered by the change of regime has exposed pre-existing vulnerabilities and undermined food security for most households. The public health system’s capacity for disease outbreak response and preparedness needs strengthening. Additional challenges include health packages that are not fully aligned with the current burden of disease in Afghanistan, insufficient healthcare staff, inadequate quality, fragmented health monitoring systems, weak health product supply chains, limited coverage for remote and rural populations, gender inequalities, and limited integration of the private sector. Afghanistan's social policy landscape is equally fragmented and under severe stress. There is no predictable or unified social protection system in place, leaving millions reliant on fragmented humanitarian support channeled through NGOs and UN agencies. Acute vulnerabilities are concentrated among women, female-headed households, persons with disabilities, internally displaced persons, and the growing population of returnees. Restrictive ITA edicts — including barriers to female education, mobility, and employment — have deepened gender inequalities and constrained access to services. In the absence of functioning state institutions, identifying, targeting, and sequencing support to the most vulnerable remains a critical operational challenge. Strengthening social protection systems, expanding access to integrated services, and addressing gender barriers are essential to halting further erosion of Afghanistan's human capital. Human capital is also constrained by low education outcomes and narrowing operational space for public sector engagement. Learning poverty in Afghanistan stands at 93 percent. Approximately 4.2 million children are out of school, with higher rates among girls. Access to early childhood education (ECE) is virtually nonexistent, with less than one percent of children enrolled. Foundational literacy and numeracy deteriorate rapidly after children leave school, perpetuating intergenerational poverty and feeding directly into the labor market. The share of youth not in education, employment, or training (NEET) reached 44 percent in 2021, and employers consistently cite skills gaps as a binding constraint on growth. The operational space for engagement in public education has narrowed significantly since 2021, with restrictions on girls' participation in secondary and tertiary education — including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and higher education — alongside ongoing curriculum changes and the envisaged gradual transition of the community-based education (CBE) model towards community-based schools. The World Bank has continued its commitment to protect the vulnerable, help preserve human capital and key economic and social institutions, reduce the need for future humanitarian assistance, and improve gender equality outcomes. It has taken a focused approach, engaging in four priority sectors in Afghanistan, including education, livelihoods, agriculture, and health, with the aim of sustaining basic services while closely monitoring the macro-fiscal and socio-economic status on the ground through analytical work. A collapse of the health system was averted by channeling emergency funding through United Nations agencies to continue contracting with NGOs to deliver basic and essential health service packages. This was followed by the Health Emergency Response (HER) project, funded by the ARTF and the Global Financing Facility (GFF) through the World Bank. UNICEF is the implementing agency for the HER projects and will continue contracting with NGOs to deliver basic and essential health services under this mechanism through December 2026. In addition, the Bank team has been conducting a Human Development (HD) Programmatic Advisory Service and Analytics (PASA) to support the development of a Human Capital and Job Project to start in 2027. The World Bank in Afghanistan: https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/afghanistan/overview A role in an FCS (Fragile and Conflict Affected Situations) location will be a truly impactful experience! Fragility, Conflict, and Violence: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/fragilityconflictviolence Roles and Responsibilities HMAPH is seeking a Health Specialist based in Kabul, Afghanistan, to provide technical and operational support to the Human Capital and Jobs (HCJ) Program, the Health Emergency Response (HER) Program, Education Emergency Response in Afghanistan (EERA) Project and Human Development Analytics. The selected candidate’s primary focus will be to provide operational and analytical support for implementing the health-related components of the HCJ program and to support the Education and Social Policy teams in the delivery of early child development (ECD), community based education, distance learning, safety nets, skills and employment as well as certification programs, and social delivery systems leveraging lessons learned from ongoing World Bank projects. The Health Specialist will also support the implementation of the broader World Bank HNP, SP and EDUSKILLS programs in Afghanistan, including engaging with relevant technical counterparts in the Interim Taliban Administration (ITA), with local and international implementation partners and donors. The selected candidate will also support the Programmatic Advisory Service and Analytics (PASA) activities, including contributing to the generation of innovation and knowledge in the HD sector, engaging on the human capital agenda, and collaborating with other sectors to enhance the impact of upcoming projects in Afghanistan. The Health Specialist will report to the HMAPH Practice Manager and work in close collaboration with the project Task Team Leader(s) (TTLs). The Health Specialist’s work program will be roughly split 60-40 between the Health and Education/Social Policy sectors. His/her support will go beyond HCJ, and s/he will cover technical dialogue across Human Development sectors. Specific duties are outlined below. Support to Health, Nutrition and Population (HNP) Portfolio (60%) Current HNP Portfolio and Analytical Projects • Support the Task Team for the Afghanistan Health Emergency Response (HER) Project with implementation and supervision activities. • Lead on several technical components of the HER Project (Quality of Care, localization of medicines) • Support technical engagement with donors and the Interim Taliban Administration's Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) on health system cost-burden sharing. • Draft technical reports and develop analytical products for the Afghanistan Human Development PASA. • Engage with TTLs, the CMU, and development partners in technical discussions to advance financing and pivot strategies. Support on HNP components in the HCJ Program The objective of the HCJ Program is to protect human capital and promote employment through private sector-led approaches, with a focus on youth and women and will be implemented by UNICEF, AKDN and WFP. • Provide technical and project management support to the TTLs, implementation partners, and the Country Management Unit (CMU) to support a gradual pivot toward private-sector provision and to align donor priorities; • Liaise with implementation partners for the delivery of basic health and nutrition services of the HCJ Program • Engage in policy dialogues and conduct assessments to support system development and capacity building, particularly to enhance health system strengthening, including medicine localization agenda • Collaborate with counterparts from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to ensure alignment in the delivery of health services under the HCJ Program and the ADB’s NOURISH project. • Support TTLs in drafting and reviewing key project documents, such as the project operations manual and the project appraisal document, and compliance reports, during the program's implementation. • Engage with the World Bank’s HNP Global Unit to provide updates on corporate indicators and scorecard targets, including the global target to deliver quality, affordable health services to 1.5bn people by 2030. Support on Education and Social Policy Portfolio (40%) • Provide inputs and support to the TTLs of the Education and Social Policy programs, particularly in implementing the ECD, community based education, distance learning, safety nets, skills and employment and certification programs as well as social delivery systems. • Maintain active policy dialogue with ITA counterparts and international and local partners on education, cash programming and safety nets, employment support mechanisms, and social protection delivery systems, including beneficiary identification, targeting, and grievance redress. • Contribute to engagement on the human capital agenda, particularly regarding gender and inclusion, to address gender-based violence, provide psychological support, and strengthen community-based platforms. • Support program TTLs in fostering synergies across Afghanistan portfolio, and within HCJ Component 1 (Sustaining Human Services) and Component 2 (Improving Youth Skills and Employment), including coordination among the multiple implementing partners. • Collaborate with the project team to develop a unified theory of change and results framework for the HCJ project, and provide support for potential project restructuring or refinancing throughout the program lifecycle. • Engage with implementing partners to support beneficiary targeting and profiling, ensuring coordinated outreach to the most vulnerable across human capital sectors.

title: Joint Fires Operational Planner, Journeyman
description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?


At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. The Leidos Intelligence Sector combines technology-enabled services and mission software capabilities in the areas of cyber, logistics, security operations, and decision analytics to support our defense and intel customers’ mission to defend against evolving threats around the world.


Your greatest work is ahead!


The Intelligence Sector seeks highly qualified and trained Journeyman-level Joint Fires Operational Planners to support United States Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM) operations, with focus on applying principles of Joint Targeting and Operational Planning processes to secure USCYBERCOM tactical objectives, reach operational goals, and actualize strategic end-states. This vital on-site support to USCYBERCOM J3 (Operations), Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF), and Joint Task Force-Ares (JTF-ARES) underpins USCYBERCOM support to United States National Security objectives.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Provide timely, accurate, relevant Operational Planning support in the manner that best underpins and drives USCYBERCOM Joint Fires Targeting process.
  • Coordinate targeting strategy development and engagement responsibilities with supported, supporting, and partner commands such as Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), National Security Agency (NSA), other interagency organizations and other service providers to ensure that USCYBERCOM and/or Cyber Mission Forces Joint Fires requirements are implemented.
  • Develop cyber TTPs that advise future operations planners on achieving Cyberspace Operations effects within the "realm of the possible" in support of operations and exercise objectives.
  • Act as technical liaison on behalf of the USCYBERCOM Operations Directorate between capability SMEs and capability developers, capability testers, planning teams, operations support staff, and operating units during planning and operations.
  • Draft and assist in the development of USCYBERCOM joint targeting policies, procedures, and commander's targeting guidance.
  • Participate in Boards, Bureaus, Centers, Cells, and Working Groups (B2C2WGs) such as Joint Targeting Working Groups (JTWG), Joint Targeting Coordination Meetings (JTCM), and Joint Targeting Coordination Boards (JTCB), to prioritize and synchronize target requirements.
  • Prepare strike packages, Cyber fires approval packages, Information Operations target packages, and otherwise support all USCYBERCOM non-kinetic fires activities.
  • Synchronize targeting methodologies across Cyber and information-related capabilities.
  • Monitor and manage intermediate and advanced target development lists and support conduct target development, target systems analysis, and Cyber weapons capability analysis.
  • Support integration of targeting activities into the broader joint targeting cycle, including interagency coordination.
  • Facilitate the transition of Fires tasks, as appropriate to Cyber Mission Force (CMF).
  • Analyze and evaluate All-Source finished intelligence and technical data from various sources to identify Cyber threat patterns and anomalies.
  • Collaborate with operational, technical, and intelligence elements across USCYBERCOM to enhance situational awareness and threat response capabilities.
  • Maintain a current understanding of advanced persistent threats (APTs), threat actor tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), and cyber threat trends affecting national security.
  • Maintain situational awareness of, and execute on demand, Cyberspace Operations (CO) crisis plans.
  • Provide situational awareness to a range of projects, Crisis Action Teams, and current operations activities supporting Operational Planning Teams (OPTs).
  • Execute resource allocation decisions aligned with organization objectives.
  • Interpret and apply laws, regulations, policies, and guidance relevant to daily activities.
  • Communicate complex information, concepts, or ideas in a confident and well-organized manner through verbal, written, and/or visual means.

What does Leidos need from me?

  • Active Top Secret/SCI (TS/SCI) security clearance with Polygraph required.
  • BA/BS degree or higher within Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Intelligence Studies, or related field, or ability to complete degree within one year of hire. Can substitute formal education with extended experience and technical certifications. Additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  • Five to eight plus years’ experience supporting CO or intelligence operations, with a focus on support to Joint Targeting. Will accept 10 years’ experience combined across CO, Information Operations, Joint Targeting, and Operational Planning fields.
  • DoD or Intelligence Community (IC)-sponsored certification for Joint Targeting.
  • Graduate of DoD or IC-sponsored operational planning training and conversant in Joint Operations Planning process, to include all applicable foundational doctrine and methodologies.
  • Demonstrated familiarity with target management systems (e.g., MIDB, Coliseum, CAT Targeting Toolkits) supporting non-kinetic effects.
  • Working understanding of Joint Targeting Cycle and related doctrine (e.g., CJCSI 3370.01, JP 3-60).
  • DOD 8140/DOD 8570 IAT Level II Certified.
  • Strong familiarity with CO, the DoD Information Environment, and Joint Fires process.
  • Demonstrated experience working with targeting Boards and Working Groups (JTWG, JTCM, JTCB) and able to lead boards or working groups, as necessary.
  • Independently conduct intermediate target development and preliminary collateral effects analysis.
  • Broad knowledge of Blue-space Cyber capabilities and demonstrate understanding of available Cyber infrastructure or platforms to conduct Defensive (DCO) and Offensive Cyberspace Operations (OCO), as well as computer networking fundamentals and concepts, terminology, and operations of a wide range of communications media (computer and telephone networks, satellite, fiber, wireless).
  • Ability to support timely, accurate, relevant analytical production, to include documents, summaries, issue papers, talking points, and briefings.
  • Demonstrated proficiency working in a fast-paced collaborative environment, ability to proactively multi-task and meet short deadlines.
  • Strong interpersonal, critical thinking, and communication skills, including the ability to clearly convey complex and technical data to nontechnical consumers.

Favorable if you have:

  • Masters’ Degree or higher within Cybersecurity, Intelligence Studies, Information Security or related fields.
  • Deep understanding of USCYBERCOM organizational structure and mission.
  • Prior experience supporting Joint operations across multiple warfighting domains.
  • Demonstrated experience incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into operations at any level to increase efficiency and effectiveness of operational outcomes.
  • Experience with Space-enabled CO.
  • Formal training within field of Cyber Warfare and Joint Operations.
  • Familiar with art of Data Science and applicability to CO.
  • Familiar with Microsoft Power BI data visualization software.
  • Desired Certifications: DoD 8570 IAT Level II (CCNA Security, COMPTIA CySA+, COMPTIA Security + CE, GICSP, GSEC, SSCP).


This posting is for multiple opportunities ranging in years of experience. Level of opportunity including compensation, will be matched to the candidate's experience.

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

title: Director of Supply Operations
description:
We’re looking for an experienced Director of Supply Operations to lead the operational direction of Smart Supply, AI Digital’s deal management and supply curation platform. Smart Supply operates as a curation layer between programmatic supply and an advertiser’s DSP, helping improve supply quality, transparency, performance, and monetization. This is a senior leadership role for someone who combines deep programmatic and supply-side expertise with strong commercial judgment, technical understanding, and hands-on operational leadership.

Responsibilities

  • Own the day-to-day operational performance of Smart Supply, excluding direct sales.

  • Lead and develop the AdOps team, including responsibility for technical implementation.

  • Drive supply monetization, curation, supply and vendor optimization, margin improvement, and revenue growth.

  • Oversee the monetization-related Client Services / Account Management function.

  • Develop and execute structured testing approaches for new technologies, traffic sources, and monetization opportunities.

  • Review and validate test results, and guide the team in identifying additional optimization and monetization opportunities.

  • Clearly communicate what has been tested, what works, what does not work, and why.

  • Provide executive leadership with clear conclusions, recommendations, and an understanding of the limitations of different approaches.

  • Partner closely with Sales to understand market and client needs and adapt operations accordingly.

  • Collaborate with Product on product direction, testing, operational feedback, and future development.

  • Collaborate with Engineering on technical feasibility and implementation.

  • Build scalable workflows, introduce automation, and improve operational efficiency.

  • Lead hiring, team development, performance management, and organizational changes.

  • Significant leadership experience in programmatic advertising, AdTech, or a closely related programmatic technology environment.

  • Strong working knowledge of the programmatic advertising ecosystem and supply-side operations, including SSPs, bid requests, curation, monetization, vendor optimization, testing, and traffic-source evaluation.

  • Strong technical understanding of programmatic operations, with the ability to review and validate technical and operational testing results.

  • Proven experience leading teams of 20+ people, including hiring, team development, performance management, and handling terminations when necessary.

  • Proven ability to lead complex operational and technical initiatives from concept through implementation.

  • Experience improving revenue performance, margins, operational efficiency, or supply quality.

  • Strong business judgment and the ability to balance technical, operational, commercial, product, and client considerations.

  • Ability to communicate complex findings clearly and directly to C-level stakeholders.

  • Experience working with the US programmatic advertising market is strongly preferred.

  • Fluent English with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

What You Get

  • USD compensation that values your expertise.‍

  • Work from anywhere: fully remote to suit your lifestyle.‍

  • 31 days of paid time off: 21 days of annual leave + 10 days of sick leave, because your health and work-life balance matter.‍

  • Growth-focused environment: access to learning resources and clear pathways for growth.‍

  • Fun team events: virtual cooking classes, yoga sessions, team quizzes and more

  • ‍A culture of trust: we cut the red tape — results over rules always. Open talk, ownership, and getting things done together.

Hiring Flow

  • Screening Interview (45 minutes): initial conversation with a recruiter.

  • Technical Interview (up to 60 minutes): A deep dive into your functional expertise, problem-solving approach, and practical skills relevant to the role.

  • Final Interview (Up to 60 minutes): Meet with the Team Lead for an in-depth discussion of your experience and skills.

  • Interview with Co-Founder (30 minutes): A high-level conversation to explore your professional values, motivation, and how your vision aligns with the company’s mission and long-term goals.

  • Offer: if successful, you’ll receive an offer to join our team.

Location & Eligibility

This role is open to applicants from EMEA (selected countries).

Please note that we’re unable to consider applications from outside these locations.

Thanks for your understanding!

title: Automotive Lube Tech
description:
We're growing and we'd love to have you grow with us

Atlantic Coast Enterprises is seeking to hire part-time and full-time Automotive Technicians to provide top-notch service at a Jiffy Lube in Sunrise, FL. Are you looking to learn and advance your skills with a company that cares about its employees? Do you want to work in a collaborative, positive environment where humor, teamwork, and laughter are encouraged? If so, keep reading!

If this sounds like the right part-time or full-time position for you, apply today!

We offer our customers these services in the cleanest, most professional surroundings possible. title: Associate Product Specialist, Product Management, Cairo - Egypt
description:

Associate Product Specialist, Product Management, Cairo - Egypt

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist

The Opportunity:

As a data scientist, you’re excited at the prospect of unlocking the secrets held by a data set, and you’re fascinated by the possibilities presented by IoT, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. In an increasingly connected world, massive amounts of structured and unstructured data open new opportunities. As a data scientist at Booz Allen, you can help turn these complex data sets into useful information to solve global challenges. Across private and public sectors, from fraud detection to cancer research to national intelligence, we need you to help find the answers in the data.


On our team, you’ll use your analytical skills and data science knowledge to create real-world impact. You’ll work closely with your clients to understand their questions and needs and then dig into their data-rich environments to find the pieces of their information puzzle. You’ll develop algorithms and systems and use the right combination of tools and frameworks to turn sets of disparate data points into objective answers to help clients make informed decisions. Ultimately, you’ll provide a deep understanding of the data, what it all means, and how it can be used.

Work with us as we use data science for good.


Join us. The world can’t wait.

Job Description:

Trafficking Program Specialist


The Trafficking Program Specialist supports the Office on Trafficking in Persons (OTIP) in Washington, DC. The position provides technical support for the oversight and implementation of victim services programs serving foreign and domestic victims of human trafficking within the United States.


Position Duties:

  • Process requests for certification from foreign national adult victims of severe forms of human trafficking, including drafting external communications about the certification process and benefits, preparing certification letters in a timely manner, coordinating with victim service providers or representatives to deliver case management assistance to victims, updating information in the adult certification database, training anti-trafficking grantees and other stakeholders on the HHS certification process, responding to inquiries via the certification verification phone line, and providing certification statistics and data analysis.
  • Process intakes and Requests for Assistance for foreign national children who may have been subjected to a severe form of trafficking in persons.
  • Create written case summaries and analysis of trafficking concerns in accordance with the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000, as amended.
  • Seek consultation with law enforcement on foreign national child trafficking cases.
  • Prepare Eligibility and Interim Assistance Letters, which are granted to foreign national children who have or may have been subjected to human trafficking.
  • Coordinate efforts and make referrals to the National Human Trafficking Hotline.
  • Responsible for receiving and responding to inquiries submitted through the trafficking Victim Verification Line and the child trafficking line by providing technical assistance to questions related to Child Eligibility, Adult Certification, and benefits and services for foreign national victims of trafficking.
  • Assist in the preparation of written materials related to trafficking certification and eligibility of victim assistance, including reports, correspondence, briefing papers, fact sheets, memoranda, policy and procedure updates, and monthly statistical reports, including the timely preparation of recurring reports on trafficking such as reports to Congress and the President’s Interagency Task Force to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons.
  • Attend intra-and inter-agency meetings regarding government-wide and private sector anti-trafficking initiatives.
  • Respond to telephonic and electronic (email) inquiries from victims/survivors of trafficking and victim advocates and legal representatives working on behalf of victims/survivors seeking certification and eligibility letters.
  • Input and track case status in an online case management system.
  • Provide input to improve work processes and efficiencies including technological innovations.
  • Develop and deliver trainings relevant to the Child Eligibility and Adult Certification processes at conferences and meetings.
  • Other duties, as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Requires a bachelor's degree in social work or related discipline with 5 years of related experience (3 years of experience required with master’s degree).
  • Experience working with foreign national populations preferred.
  • Case management experience preferred.
  • Child protection and child welfare experience preferred.
  • Direct experience working with/for anti-trafficking programs preferred.
  • Strong organizational and analytical skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Additional Requirements:

  • This position requires an existing Public Trust or the ability to obtain one.
  • This position is based in Washington, DC and employees are required to report on-site 3 days per week.

Materials Specialists are responsible for the execution of product handling/logistics in a cGMP environment. Join us. The world can’t wait.

title: Associate, GPS Active Strategy & Innovation
description:
About this role

Your team:


The Global Product Solutions (GPS) business innovates and curates all of BlackRock’s investment solutions to bring the right products and solutions, in the right way, at the right time, to help our clients meet their goals. The team is responsible for oversight of active and index strategies across ETFs, mutual funds, and separate accounts, spanning liquid and illiquid assets in both public and private markets. As a member of this team, you will help to drive the next phase of growth for our global product platform and the entire firm.


Your role and impact:


As part of the Americas Active team within GPS, you will cultivate deep product and industry expertise to innovate transformative products and solutions, and commercialize BlackRock’s extensive active product platform. This individual will drive the product agenda for each asset class across the liquid active business by developing long-term growth strategy, uncovering new innovation opportunities aligned with evolving client needs and continued growth of Active ETFs, and driving commercialization of the entire Active platform through sales enablement, thought leadership and direct client engagement.


This is a multifaceted, high-profile role that requires frequent interaction at the most senior levels of the firm to change the face of our product set. You will work closely with global investors, client-facing teams, product marketing, legal, and other operational partners on exciting projects that drive significant growth of BlackRock’s active business. The successful candidate will be an indispensable partner to these teams and will benefit from inclusion in a large, globally diverse product organization, with access to a broad range of skills and expertise that contribute to a deep understanding of client motivations, strategy development and fund structuring across regions and sales channels.


Your responsibilities:

  • Crafting and implementing asset class and product platform growth strategy aligned to firmwide priorities alongside partners on distribution and investment teams
  • Leading industry and competitive analysis to identify client trends and uncover commercial opportunities to position BlackRock’s active products and solutions in key client segments
  • Bringing creative thinking and analytical insight to new product and wrapper innovation across wealth and institutional channels, including commercial testing and prioritization of new concepts
  • Conducting fund range analysis to assess the health and salability of the existing active product platform and, where appropriate, recommending changes to improve commercial appeal
  • Defining the asset class product agenda by mapping, guiding, and tracking products throughout their lifecycle, managing seed capital allocations, and helping to set annual sales targets
  • Building presentations and memos to communicate strategic plans, ongoing progress and final recommendations to senior audiences across product, investment and client organizations
  • Supporting leaders of the Americas Active product team in client and board engagements

What are we looking for?

  • Bachelor’s degree required; MBA, CFA designation, or demonstrated progress toward the CFA designation (e.g., Level I or II candidate) preferred
  • 3+ years of experience in asset management, product strategy, investment product development, investment management, consulting, or a related field.
  • Knowledge and understanding of investment management products and liquid asset classes
  • A relationship builder with outstanding written and verbal communication skills
  • Proven ability to lead sophisticated, cross-functional projects
  • High energy self-starter with strong integrity and a high degree of creativity
  • Strong data analytics and visualization skills are crucial

title: Security Operations Centre Assistant
description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

The Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) is responsible for providing leadership, operational support, and oversight of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS) globally. As a global leader in security risk management principles, UNDSS enables the safe and effective delivery of United Nations programmes and activities in the most complex and challenging environments, while maximizing precious resources, To this end, the work of the Department is aligned under a clear mission, to enable United Nations system programme activities through trusted security leadership and solutions. This is a unique opportunity to join a diverse, dynamic, and exciting organization gaining unique and valuable experience where security provides great value. Besides the opportunity to gain new skills and further advance security expertise, this position offers a fulfilling environment that gives you satisfaction by contributing directly or indirectly to peace and security, human rights, and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. For more information on the Department, and how we make an impact on the world in enabling the achievement of SDGs, visit .

UNDSS Sudan is supporting the UN entities and International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs) and International Organizations (IOS) so as to enable the conduct of humanitarian relief programmes. UNDSS seeks to fill a number of posts across Sudan. Successful candidates must be able to work within one of these locations. Additionally, successful candidates must be prepared to relocate to other parts of the country and travel on official business, based on evolving humanitarian planning in Sudan.

Scope of Work

The Security Operations Centre Assistant (SOC Assistant) works in close collaboration with the UNDSS Field Security Coordination Officers/ Field Security Associates and other UN personnel (especially Security Wardens) in providing support on telecommunications-related issues.

Duties and Responsibilities

The key functions will include:

  1. Support daily operations:
  • Professionally operate and communicate using UN standard telecommunications facilities, including VHF and HF radio networks, to receive dispatch and relay messages as required.
  • Answer all calls, whether on radio or telephone, promptly and efficiently.
  • Maintain radio contact with all radio users, stations, and vehicles operating on the United Nations inter-agency radio network(s) under their responsibility.
  • Maintain regular communications with staff in the field and HQ, utilizing HF / VHF / Sat phone or any other forms of telecommunication’s equipment and methods at your disposal.
  • Track all missions and advise on all security-related issues.
  • Provide initial response to all emergency communications to the radio room as appropriate.
  • Monitor the news 24/7 and report security incidents and any accident involving UN staff.

2. Ensure information-sharing:

  • Advise all concerned staff members of important incoming radio messages.
  • Type, distribute, and respond by a variety of means - email, phone, messenger - and log accurately all incoming/outgoing radio/phone messages to concerned personnel to keep a detailed record of all radio traffic, telephone, and messenger messages that pass through the radio room.
  • Disseminate security information and advisories to all agency security officers and security focal points.
  • Ensure efficient communications and information flow for all units and agencies.

3. Monitor compliance with security communications system protocols:

  • Ensure all network users are complying with standard radio procedures, and call signs and radio discipline are strictly maintained.
  • Implement standard UN Call sign systems, vehicle tracking procedures, and Standard Operating Procedures at all radio rooms.

4. Support information management:

  • Have access to Electronic Daily Staff List at all times. In case of an emergency immediately inform the Field Security Coordination Officers and the radio room supervisor and act accordingly.
  • Ensure the radio room has updated staff lists with contact details, and vehicle lists.
  • Establish daily contact with UNAFP security to confirm any changes in UN staff movements within their area of responsibility before staff starts the mission.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of all relevant messages sent and received through the radio room communications systems.

5. Ensure functional operability of the SOC:

  • Ensure radio rooms are adequately equipped and have up-to-date documentation.
  • Maintain properly all radio networks and communications equipment at the user level, reporting problems promptly to relevant staff.
  • Analyse the communications requirements, recommend new systems and/or enhancements in the functionality of the existing systems.
  • Immediately advise the radio room supervisor or Field Security Coordination Officers on faults in the telecommunications networks and undertake all necessary action to provide a prompt re-establishment of service.
  • Assist the ICT officer in the installation and arrangement of equipment and fixtures where needed.
  • Provide basic technical support for communications equipment in the field.

6. Perform other functions as may be required:

  • Train UN’s implementing partners on a per-need basis and as time permits.
  • Work closely with other agencies telecoms services.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL l: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL l: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL l: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity and uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL l: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL l: Appreciates/respects differences, aware of unconscious bias, confronts discrimination.

Cross-functional & Technical competencies

Business Management:

Digital Awareness and Literacy.

Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skilfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed.

Business Management:

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management.

Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Security Services:

Security Incident Management & Monitoring:

Ability to provide adequate response to security incidents/events.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Completed secondary education. Certificate in radio telecommunications is an added value.

Experience:

  • A minimum of 4 years (with secondary education) and 1 year (with a Bachelor’s degree) of experience in radio communications. Good knowledge of computer applications (MS Office, Internet).
  • Knowledge of hardware installation and maintenance is desirable.
  • Experience as radio operator, call agent or related is desirable.
  • Excellent knowledge of Codan VHF and Motorola VHF systems, knowledge of Selective calling and SELV- and programming of the same is required.

Required skills:

Strong computer skills, including proficiency in MS Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

  • Previous UN experience.
  • Proficiency in operating HF and VHF radios.
  • Familiarity with the host country's safety regulations.
  • Valid driver's licence.
  • Willingness to travel.
  • Physical fitness.

Required language(s):

Fluency in English and Arabic is required.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

title: Data Engineer, Senior
description:

Ever-expanding technology like IoT, machine learning, and artificial intelligence means that there’s more structured and unstructured data available today than ever before. As a data engineer, you know that organizing data can yield pivotal insights when it’s gathered from disparate sources. We need an experienced data engineer like you to help our clients find answers in their data to impact important missions, from fraud detection to cancer research, to national intelligence.


As a Data Engineer at Booz Allen, you’ll help build advanced technology solutions and implement data engineering activities on some of the most mission-driven projects in the industry. You’ll deploy and develop pipelines and platforms that organize and make disparate data meaningful.


Here, you’ll work with and guide a multi-disciplinary team of analysts, data engineers, developers, and data consumers in a fast-paced, agile environment. You’ll use your experience in analytical exploration and data examination while you manage the assessment, design, building, and maintenance of scalable platforms for your clients.

You Have:

  • 6+ years of experience designing data warehouse or data lake, RESTful API models, event processing, or business intelligence for software systems
  • Experience building scalable ETL or ELT data pipelines, automating large-scale batch and streaming data workflows, and parsing structured, unstructured, or event-streaming data
  • Experience with coding in software programming languages, including Postgres, SQL, Python, Scala, Spark, or Java
  • Experience using Apache Spark, Apache NiFi, or Databricks
  • Experience performing tuning on data lake architecture to optimize cloud storage and pipeline performance
  • Experience with data management solutions that address aspects of data catalog, data usage, governance policies, and lifecycle management
  • Top Secret clearance
  • Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of experience designing, developing, operationalizing, and maintaining data systems, or 12+ years of experience designing, developing, operationalizing, and maintaining data systems in lieu of a degree

  • 4+ years of experience using and developing data systems with AWS and Microsoft Azure cloud data products such as AWS EMR, AWS Glue, Azure Dataverse, Azure Data Factory, and Power Apps
  • Experience with distributed data or computing tools, including Apache Spark, Apache NiFi, AirFlow, Databricks, Snowflake, Redshift, or BigQuery
  • Experience with federal information system policies, including NIST 800.53 and FISMA, data security, access controls, and data protection techniques
  • Experience creating and improving continuous automation across multiple technical stacks, and automating CD/CD pipelines with tools such as Jenkins or GitHub

MOVE by GoodLife Kids

GoodLife Kids Foundation (GLKF) enables and supports kids and youth with autism and intellectual disabilities through physical activity and fitness. Our vision is that all kids and youth with autism and intellectual disabilities experience the joys and benefits of being active.

The MOVE by GoodLife Kids program is a free physical activity and fitness program for youth ages 12 – 21 years with autism and intellectual disabilities. MOVE by GoodLife Kids Program class runs In Person and Virtually across Canada up to three times per week. MOVE Classes incorporate social time, workouts, dancing, and mental wellness.



What is a MOVE Coach?

Each MOVE Coach is responsible for coaching and delivering exceptional fitness programming for the MOVE by GoodLife Kids program, through adaptive and progressive workouts.

You will play an important role helping with the continued development of this national program. You will provide input and recommendations as to what works for your Participants and try out recommendations from the rest of the coaching team.

GLKF will provide training on how to support youth with disabilities – if you have a passion for helping EVERYBODY live a fit and healthy good life, this could be the job for you!

You will forecast, select, organize and assign the personnel, facilities and equipment needed to produce programs or program segments. This includes managing logistical planning across pre-production, production and post-production phases while meeting cross-platform formatting and delivery requirements. Although general direction will be provided, this role requires strong independent judgment and initiative.
